title: Coordinate end-of-season gear bag/bin collection
details:
Collect gear bags and bins from teams, retrieve batting cage nets and banners, and complete concessions/upstairs cleanout.

At the close of the playing season the Equipment Manager reclaims all shared league gear so nothing is lost or left to weather over the offseason. This means pulling gear bags and locked bins back from every field, retrieving batting-cage nets and sponsor/field banners, and finishing the concessions and upstairs storage cleanout. Consolidating everything now (typically staged at Douglas) protects the league's investment and sets up the fall inventory.
steps: Notify head coaches of the return deadline and confirm each field's bin combination/key so bins can be opened and emptied.
Collect gear bags and locked bins from every field, verifying balls are back in the bins and bins are re-locked.
Take down and roll up batting-cage nets and remove banners before winter weather.
Complete the concessions/snack-shack and upstairs storage cleanout, clearing out perishables and organizing shelving.
Transport all gear to the central staging location (e.g. Douglas) and group it by set (Tee Ball, AA/AAA/Majors) for the offseason.
Note any missing, stolen, or damaged items so they can be added to the replacement list.

title: Order bat/ball/team equipment replacements
details: After the fall inventory identifies gaps, the Equipment Manager purchases replacement bats, balls, and shared team equipment for the next season within board-approved caps (bats up to $2,000; balls $1,400-$2,500). Ordering in the offseason ensures gear arrives before winter prep and pre-season staging. The league's annual {{equipmentVendor}} sponsorship credit and partner discount code should be applied to stretch the budget.
steps: Build the replacement order from the inventory needs list, splitting practice vs. season baseballs/softballs and bats by division.
Keep the bat total within the ~$2,000 cap and balls within the $1,400-$2,500 range approved by the board.
Apply the annual {{equipmentVendor}} sponsorship equipment credit using the league partner discount code.
Place the order with the league vendor and confirm expected delivery ahead of winter/pre-season prep.
Submit receipts to the Treasurer for reimbursement or record against the approved spending motion.

title: Prepare equipment inventory and needs report
details:
Inventory bats, baseballs, catcher's gear, mowers/tractors, and bins; assess storage security and present needs to the board.

The Equipment Manager compiles a full inventory of bats, baseballs, catcher's gear, mowers/tractors, and bins, assesses how securely gear is stored, and presents the resulting needs to the board. This report drives the season's equipment spending motion and flags recurring problems such as bin theft. It is typically presented at a winter organizational/board meeting alongside registration and uniform planning.
steps: Count on-hand bats, baseballs/softballs, helmets, catcher's gear, mowers/tractors, and bins by division.
Assess storage security, noting bin theft history and whether gear should move to the snack shack as a contingency.
Draft the needs list with target quantities (e.g. ~24 helmets tee ball/player pitch, 12 each Majors/Minors, 20 dozen practice + 30 dozen season baseballs, a dozen bats each sport) and cost estimates.
Prepare a short board report tying quantities to a dollar estimate for the spending motion.
Present the report at the board meeting and answer questions to support the equipment purchase motion.

title: Complete fall equipment inventory
details:
Conduct the fall inventory of all playing equipment to establish on-hand stock and replacement list.

The fall inventory establishes the league's true on-hand stock once all gear has been collected from the fields at season's end. Counting everything now produces the baseline replacement list that feeds offseason purchasing and the winter board spending motion. Doing it in the fall gives enough lead time to order and receive gear before the next season.
steps: Gather all collected bins, bags, and gear at the central storage location and open every bin.
Count and record bats, baseballs/softballs, helmets, catcher's gear, tees, nets, and misc items (bat grips, bownets) by division.
Flag worn, damaged, or missing items and set them aside from usable stock.
Compile the replacement list with target on-hand quantities for the coming season.
Store all usable gear securely in labeled, locked bins for the offseason.

title: Purchase winter season-prep equipment
details: During the winter the Equipment Manager places the major season-prep order once the board has approved equipment spending. This covers helmets, catcher's gear, baseballs/softballs, bats, tees, and nets identified as gaps in the fall inventory. Ordering in winter ensures gear is on hand to stage and distribute before games begin in the spring.
steps: Convert the fall inventory needs list into a concrete winter purchase order by division.
Prioritize lower-level catcher's gear (ages 7-8 and 9-10) and helmet counts, which are recurring shortfalls.
Order helmets, catcher's gear, baseballs/softballs, bats, tees, and nets within the approved spending amount.
Apply the {{equipmentVendor}} sponsorship credit/discount code and confirm delivery timelines before pre-season prep.
Log the purchase and submit receipts to the Treasurer against the board-approved motion.

title: Run pre-season equipment inventory and purchasing
details:
Complete pre-season inventory and order helmets, catcher's gear, balls, bats, tees, and nets to fill gaps before games.

Just before the season the Equipment Manager re-checks stock against final registration numbers and fills any remaining gaps in helmets, catcher's gear, balls, bats, tees, and nets. This last-mile inventory catches shortfalls the winter order missed once team counts are set, so every field is fully equipped before games. It typically happens in the weeks leading into spring practices and Opening Day.
steps: Reconcile on-hand gear against final registration and team counts by division.
Identify any remaining shortfalls in helmets, catcher's gear, balls, bats, tees, and nets.
Place a final gap-filling order with enough lead time to arrive before staging.
Sort and pre-stage gear into per-field sets (Tee Ball, AA/AAA/Majors) at the central staging location.
Confirm each field's bin/lock and combination are ready for distribution.

title: Prepare equipment spending motion for board
details: The Equipment Manager works with the president to draft the team/field equipment purchase list and a spending motion (e.g. up to {{amount}}) for board approval. Formalizing purchasing authority by motion lets gear be bought at the discretion of the president and equipment manager within a set cap. This is presented at a winter board meeting so orders can be placed in time for the season.
steps: Turn the inventory needs report into an itemized purchase list with per-category cost estimates.
Set a not-to-exceed amount (e.g. {{amount}}) and draft the motion language granting spending discretion to the president and equipment manager.
Review the list and motion with the president before the meeting.
Present the motion at the board meeting and record the second and vote in the minutes.
Proceed with ordering once the motion carries, tracking spend against the approved cap.

title: Set up Tee Ball / Coach Pitch field bins
details:
Assemble and place gear bins, helmets, and equipment on Tee Ball and Coach Pitch fields before the season begins.

Before the Tee Ball and Coach Pitch season opens, the equipment team assembles and places gear bins, helmets, and equipment on each of those fields. This is often done at a bin-assembly day at Douglas with pop-up tents used to organize a set per field before distribution. Getting bins staged and delivered ensures every young-division field is ready for the first practices and games.
steps: Assemble the gear bins and sort helmets, bats, tees, balls, and buckets into a set per Tee Ball/Coach Pitch field.
Use pop-up tents at the staging site (e.g. Douglas behind Subway) to organize each field's set.
Deliver and place each set at its assigned field, arranging equipment sharing where a field lacks its own gear.
Set bin lock combinations and record them for coach distribution.
Confirm with the Tee Ball/Coach Pitch VP that every field is stocked before the first practice.

title: Place ball order and stock season equipment
details:
Order baseballs/softballs and stock tees, buckets, helmets, and catcher's gear for in-season use.

Early in the season the Equipment Manager places the main baseball/softball order and stocks each field's consumables and shared gear. Each field is set with roughly two buckets of ~48 baseballs plus tees, buckets, helmets, and catcher's gear for in-season use. Keeping balls replenished matters because baseballs are the most frequently lost and stolen item.
steps: Place the season baseball/softball order (practice and game balls) based on the approved quantities.
Stock each field with roughly two buckets of ~48 baseballs (about 96 total), numbered in groups.
Distribute tees, buckets, helmets, and catcher's gear to fields by division set.
Remind coaches to sort and recover balls at the end of each practice and report missing balls for replacement.
Track ball replacement needs through the season and reorder as buckets run low.

title: Recruit equipment setup volunteers
details:
Send the equipment setup volunteer request and organize a bin-assembly day with pop-up tents per field.

The Equipment Manager recruits a small crew (typically 3-4 volunteers) to help assemble gear bins and organize a season setup/bin-assembly day. The work happens at a central field (e.g. Douglas) using pop-up tents to organize a gear set for each field. Recruiting help spreads the workload and gets all fields equipped quickly right before the season.
steps: Set the bin-assembly day date, time, and location (e.g. Douglas, a 12-2 window).
Send the equipment setup volunteer request asking for 3-4 helpers, noting pop-up tents will organize gear per field.
Confirm volunteers and share what to bring and where to meet.
Run the assembly day: build bins, sort gear into per-field sets under the tents, and stage for distribution.
Thank volunteers and note anyone willing to help again for future setups.

title: Collect, sort, and store end-of-season gear
details:
Gather gear bags, bins, cage nets, and uniforms; sort and store securely for the offseason.

As the season winds down the Equipment Manager gathers gear bags, bins, batting-cage nets, and returned uniforms, then sorts and stores everything securely for the offseason. Consolidating and locking down gear prevents loss and theft, which have been recurring problems with unlocked bins. This collection feeds the subsequent fall inventory.
steps: Notify coaches of the gear return deadline and collect gear bags, bins, and any issued equipment from each field.
Retrieve batting-cage nets and gather returned uniforms.
Sort gear into division sets and separate damaged/missing items from usable stock.
Store all gear in locked bins at the central storage location, keeping baseballs secured given prior theft.
Record shortfalls and damage to seed the fall inventory and replacement list.

title: Schedule equipment inventory and recruit volunteers
details:
Set the next inventory date and line up volunteers to count and organize equipment.

The Equipment Manager sets the offseason inventory date and lines up volunteers to count and organize the collected gear. Scheduling the count and a helper crew ensures the inventory gets done efficiently and produces an accurate on-hand list. This is the lead-in to the fall inventory and replacement planning.
steps: Pick an inventory date once all gear has been collected and staged.
Send a volunteer request for helpers to count and organize equipment on that date.
Prepare inventory sheets grouped by division and item type (bats, balls, helmets, catcher's gear, tees, nets, bins).
Confirm volunteers, location, and access to the storage bins/combinations.
Run the count, tally usable vs. replacement items, and compile the results for the needs report.

title: Compile end-of-season field cleanup priority list
details:
Walk each field (Douglas, Penney, Pennell, Newbegin, Intervale, Russell, {{townC}}) and list needed fall work: fencing, base paths, mounds, dugouts, drag, aerate/fertilize.

As the season winds down, the grounds crew walks every {{leagueAbbrev}} field to inventory the fall work each one needs, since fall is the best window for major field work (spring is rainy and often frozen). This priority list feeds the board's fall maintenance planning, equipment budgeting, and volunteer work-day scheduling. It should capture fencing, base paths, mounds, dugouts, dragging, and turf care (aerate/fertilize) field by field.
steps: Walk each field in turn: Douglas, Penney, Pennell, Newbegin, Intervale, Russell, and the {{townC}} fields.
At each field, note needed work in categories: fencing, base paths/infield mix, mounds and batter's boxes, dugouts, dragging, and aerate/fertilize.
Flag capital-scale items separately (e.g. Douglas batting cage rebuild, Intervale fencing/dugouts, field strips) so the board can scope them as projects.
Note which fields are shared or town/school-owned (Pennell, Newbegin, Memorial, St. Gregory's, {{townC}}) so access and owner coordination can be arranged.
Rank items by safety and playability impact (base paths clear of weeds, rocks, and large holes first) versus cosmetic work.
Compile the list into a single field-by-field summary and bring it to the fall board meeting for the Fields (Fall Maintenance & Planning) discussion.

title: Scope fall field improvement projects and costs
details:
Draft scope and rough budgets for Intervale, Bennett Rd, Douglass, lights, batting cages, and 50/70 conversions for board discussion.

The grounds crew turns the fall priority list into scoped projects with rough budgets so the board can decide what to fund and authorize by motion. Historically this has covered Intervale, Bennett Rd, Douglas, lights, batting cages, and 50/70 conversions. Each project needs a rough cost and materials plan because field, equipment, and capital spending is approved by board motion, second, and vote.
steps: Draft a short scope for each candidate project: Intervale, Bennett Rd, Douglas, lights, batting cages, and 50/70 conversions.
Gather rough budgets and quotes (e.g. batting cage net ~$700, metal shed ~$550, mowers ~$1,900 each, fencing materials, infield mix) from suppliers and contractors.
Note funding sources for capital items: grants ({{landTrust}}, SK/Stephen King grant, Alfond), banner/fence-screen sponsorships, and GoFundMe.
Identify which items are routine (fertilizer, dragging) versus capital actions needing a specific dollar-cap motion (e.g. {{amount}} to convert Penney to 50/70).
Package the scope and budgets into a board discussion document and present at a fall meeting for motions authorizing spend.

title: Order fall fertilizer and schedule aeration
details:
Purchase fall fertilizer (up to ~{{amount}} for Douglas/Penney) and arrange aeration before ground freezes.

Fall is the right time to feed and aerate the turf at the league's primary fields, Douglas and Penney, before the ground freezes. Fertilizer spend is a routine field expense approved by board motion (historically up to ~{{amount}} for Douglas/Penney). Getting the fertilizer down and the fields aerated in fall sets up healthier grass and better drainage for the following season.
steps: Confirm the board has approved the fertilizer purchase (typically a motion for up to ~{{amount}} for Douglas and Penney).
Order fall fertilizer for Douglas and Penney and coordinate pickup/supply (historically via a local supplier such as Bark Bros).
Schedule aeration for both fields before the ground freezes, arranging equipment or a contractor.
Apply fertilizer and complete aeration together where possible so nutrients reach the root zone.
Record the spend and completion so it can be reported at the next board meeting under fall field maintenance.

title: Service and winterize grounds equipment
details:
Service mowers/tractors, drags, and sheds; secure equipment storage for winter.

Before winter, the grounds crew services and stores the league's mowers, tractors, drags, and sheds so equipment is ready and protected through the off-season. {{leagueAbbrev}} keeps lawn tractors, trimmers, and sheds on site at each field, and has purchased multiple mowers and tractors (including three tractors bought with Intervale grant funds), so this is real fleet upkeep. Secure storage also matters because the league has repeatedly experienced theft at Douglas.
steps: Inventory the fleet: lawn tractors/mowers (including the grant-funded tractors), drags, trimmers, and hand tools at each field.
Service each mower and tractor (oil, blades, fuel stabilizer, batteries) and repair or note drags and trailers needing work.
Clean and stow drags, rakes, and trimmers in the on-site sheds/bins.
Confirm sheds and equipment bins are locked and secure for winter; relocate at-risk gear (e.g. balls from Douglas) into a snack shack or off-site if theft has been a problem.
Flag any equipment needing replacement so it can be budgeted in the fall equipment discussion.

title: Advance Douglass batting cage / infield mix plan
details:
Get quotes and materials plan for the Douglass batting cage (net, poles) and infield mix work.

The Douglas batting cage was slated for a full rebuild (new net, poles, structure, turf) and the infield needs substantial mix and top-dressing. This task gathers quotes and a materials plan so the board can authorize the project by motion. Historically the board authorized a contractor (Ruddley Emerson) to proceed at a cost not to exceed {{amount}} with a named point person, so a solid scope and quote are prerequisites.
steps: Get a quote for the batting cage rebuild covering net, poles/structure, turf, and gravel/sand (historically ~55x12x12 net, later 15' wide x 65' long turf).
Call Dig Safe before any post excavation and check on bringing power to the cage.
Price and plan the infield mix needed to top-dress the Douglas infield.
Compare options (e.g. reuse of an available donated net, used turf) to reduce cost.
Assign a point person and bring the quote to the board for a motion authorizing a not-to-exceed amount (e.g. {{amount}}).

title: Take down banners, cages, and complete fall cleanup
details:
Remove field banners and batting cage nets and finish end-of-season field cleanup.

At the true end of the season the grounds crew retrieves the outfield sponsor banners and takes down the batting cage nets (Penney and Pennell) so they don't weather over winter, and finishes end-of-season field cleanup. This protects league assets (banners and nets are paid sponsorship/equipment items) and closes out the fields. It typically runs alongside equipment inventory and fall turf work.
steps: Retrieve all outfield/fence sponsor banners and store them dry for reuse next season.
Take down batting cage nets at Penney and Pennell (and any others) and store them out of the weather.
Do a final leaf, trash, and debris cleanup pass on each field.
Coordinate takedown with the batting cage crew (e.g. Pennell cage takedown historically scheduled around 11am on a set date).
Confirm bins and sheds are locked, and note any missing or damaged nets/banners for the equipment inventory.

title: Order infield mix, fertilizer, and cage materials for spring
details:
Line up spring materials (infield mix, fertilizer, cage/net supplies) and confirm mower/drag readiness.

In late winter the grounds crew lines up the consumables and materials needed for spring field prep so nothing holds up opening the fields. This includes infield mix, fertilizer, and cage/net supplies, plus confirming the mowers and drags are ready to run. Ordering early matters because spring is short and rainy, and materials deliveries (e.g. infield mix drops at Douglas) drive short-notice work days.
steps: Compile the spring materials list: infield mix (Douglas/Russell especially), fertilizer, and cage/net supplies.
Place orders and schedule delivery timing so mix arrives when volunteer crews can spread it.
Confirm mowers, tractors, and drags are serviced and ready after winter storage.
Verify batting cage materials (net, poles, turf) are on hand or ordered for spring installation.
Coordinate with the board/treasurer so any spend is within approved motions before ordering.

title: Schedule and staff spring field cleanup days
details:
Set cleanup day dates by town/field, recruit volunteers, and send the field work day notice with tool/task lists.

This is the flagship spring field cleanup effort that gets every field playable before the season opens, typically the weekend before games start with a rain-date backup (e.g. Field Cleanup 4/12 with a 4/26 rain date in 2026). The crew sets dates by town/field, recruits volunteers, and sends a work-day notice with tool and task lists. Cleanup focuses on raking leaves, clearing trash, and working infield surfaces so base paths are clear of weeds, rocks, and large holes.
steps: Set the primary cleanup day and a rain date, and assign specific fields by town ({{townA}}, {{townB}}, {{townC}}).
List each field's tasks and tools: leaf/steel rakes, shovels, edgers, weed whackers, leaf blowers, pruning shears for bittersweet, and drags for the infield.
Assign teams to fields and communicate assignments (historically teams were told their field a few days ahead, e.g. by the Thursday before).
Send the Field Work Day notice with date, time (e.g. 12-2pm), field addresses, task list, and what to bring; note you go rain or shine.
Include division-specific fields (Douglas, Russell, Pennell, Memorial, St. Gregory's Tee Ball, Intervale) and note that players are encouraged to help.
Post a follow-up if any cleanups are postponed to the rain date.

title: Install field locks and begin in-season mowing rotation
details:
Install locks, set drag/mowing schedule, and remind coaches to drag fields and rake mounds/batter's boxes after use.

As opening week arrives, the crew stocks and secures the field equipment bins, distributes lock combinations to adults only, and starts the recurring mowing and dragging rotation. Bin combinations must not be shared because the league has had theft in prior years. The crew also reminds coaches to drag fields and rake mounds and batter's boxes after every use to keep fields playable all season.
steps: Assemble and stock the gear bins for each field before opening week (historically a 3-4 volunteer setup at Douglas the weekend before).
Install/verify locks on bins, sheds, and gates, and distribute combinations to assigned adults only, reminding them not to share due to past theft.
Note shared-field arrangements (e.g. St. Gregory's third field shares gear; lock the porta potty at night).
Set the mowing and dragging schedule across fields for the season.
Send the field maintenance reminder to coaches: drag the field, rake and level the batter's boxes, and smooth the mound after each game or practice.

title: Progress field conversion/improvement projects
details: During the season the crew advances active capital and improvement projects as weather and materials allow: the Fenway/Green Monster wall at Penney/Morrison Field, Intervale, batting cages, and field strips. Some of this is short-notice work driven by material deliveries, using volunteer crews with lawn tractors, trailers, shovels, and rakes. Getting fields tip-top before playoffs is a common driver.
steps: Track the status of each in-season project: Fenway wall (Penney/Morrison), Intervale, batting cages, and field strips.
When materials arrive (e.g. infield mix delivered to Douglas), organize a short-notice work crew with a start time and a text chain to coordinate.
Bring the right tools: lawn tractor with trailer, tractor with turf tires if available, shovels, and rakes.
Re-cut infield lines and spread infield mix (Douglas and Russell have been done this way before playoffs).
Work around the game/practice schedule at each field and continue on additional days as windows allow.

title: Coordinate summer field maintenance staffing
details:
Confirm ground crew volunteers for ongoing summer mowing and dragging and recognize the crew.

Mid-summer the crew confirms the volunteers who keep fields mowed and dragged through the back half of the season and into all-stars, and recognizes the people doing the work. Ongoing maintenance is largely volunteer-driven: after every game and practice fields should be dragged, and the home team is responsible for field maintenance. Keeping a reliable crew ensures fields stay playable and setup time stays short.
steps: Confirm the roster of ground crew volunteers for ongoing summer mowing and dragging across the fields.
Fill any gaps by recruiting parents, reminding them that any fan, parent, or player can grab a rake or drag.
Reinforce that the home team drags and maintains the field at every game, with visiting teams welcome to help.
Keep mowing and dragging on a regular rotation so weeds stay out of the infields.
Publicly thank and recognize the ground crew volunteers for their work.

title: Plan fall cleanup and grounds equipment needs
details: As the season closes, the grounds coordinator assesses the state of mowers, sheds, bleachers, and drag/trailer needs and sets the fall cleanup schedule. This assessment feeds the fall equipment discussion and budget at the board meeting and lines up the end-of-season work days. It's the planning counterpart to the actual fall cleanup and winterizing that follow.
steps: Assess the condition of mowers/tractors, sheds, bleachers, and drags/trailers across all fields.
Note replacement or repair needs (e.g. additional shed, new drag or trailer) with rough costs for the equipment discussion.
Set the fall cleanup schedule and identify which fields need the most work.
Coordinate a fall equipment inventory day (historically ~11am-2pm at Douglas) with volunteers.
Bring the equipment needs and cleanup plan to the fall board meeting for discussion and any spending motions.

title: Close out and pay for Douglass batting cage project
details:
Verify batting cage completion at Douglass and process the final payout.

Once the Douglas batting cage is complete, the crew verifies the finished work against the authorized scope and processes the final contractor payout. The board authorized the installation at a not-to-exceed amount with a named point person, so closeout confirms the work is done before the treasurer pays. This closes the multi-year cage rebuild (posts, net, turf, gravel/sand).
steps: Verify the batting cage is complete at Douglas: posts set, net hung, turf, gravel/sand, and structure finished.
Confirm the final cost is within the board's authorized not-to-exceed amount and matches the contractor's invoice.
Reconcile any league-purchased materials (pipes/turf ordered separately, stored to avoid theft) against the total.
Have the point person sign off, then coordinate with the treasurer to process the final payout.
Report completion and final cost to the board and update the project status.

title: Report Intervale and Douglass capital project status
details:
Prepare update on Intervale (dugouts, benches, fencing, King grant) and Douglass cage (net, turf, gravel, cement) for the board.

At the fall/winter board meetings the grounds coordinator reports on the league's two major capital efforts: Intervale (dugouts, benches, fencing, and the associated grant funding) and the Douglas cage (net, turf, gravel, cement). These updates keep the board informed on progress, spending, and grant reconciliation so it can plan the next phase. Intervale funding has combined the SK/Stephen King grant ($35K), GoFundMe, and {{landTrust}} contributions (including a final {{landTrust}} payment of $13,959).
steps: Compile Intervale status: dugout pads/concrete, benches, fencing (black vinyl-coated), old fencing removed, and containers on site.
Summarize Intervale funding and grant reconciliation (SK/King grant, GoFundMe, {{landTrust}} budget and the final {{amount}} payment).
Compile Douglas cage status: net, turf, gravel, cement/posts, and remaining spring work.
Note outstanding work and next-phase needs (e.g. infield dragging at Intervale, top-dressing at Douglas).
Present the combined capital update at the board meeting for discussion and any authorizations.

title: Compile end-of-season survey for board retrospective
details:
Build and distribute the post-season survey, then compile results (positives, negatives, complaints) for the board's season retrospective.

After the spring season wraps, {{leagueAbbrev}} surveys all families to gather feedback across every division for the season retrospective. The information officer builds the Google Form, blasts it to the full league, and compiles the responses into positives, negatives, and complaints for the board. This feedback drives fall planning decisions on registration timing, division structure, and volunteer needs.
steps: Build or reuse the season survey as a Google Form (forms.gle link) covering all divisions for the April-June spring season.
Have the board proof the draft survey before it goes out, then send it to the entire league via the registration system email blast (subject like '{{leagueAbbrev}} - Spring Season League Survey').
Leave the survey open a couple of weeks and send at least one reminder to boost response counts.
Export responses and summarize them into positives, negatives, and complaints, broken out by division where possible.
Package the summary for the board's late-summer retrospective (agenda items like 'End of Season Survey Review' and 'Recap of Positives and Negatives').

title: Present season recap and survey feedback
details:
Summarize end-of-season survey feedback and the season recap for the board during fall planning.

During fall planning, the information officer presents the compiled survey feedback and a recap of the completed season to the board. This turns raw family feedback into actionable decisions ahead of setting the next season's registration date and calendar. It typically feeds a late-fall board meeting where registration timing and volunteer sign-up plans are locked in.
steps: Consolidate the compiled survey results (positives, negatives, complaints) into a concise recap deck or one-pager.
Pair survey themes with season outcomes (registration counts, division participation, notable issues) to frame recommendations.
Add the recap to the fall board meeting agenda alongside items like 'Volunteer Opportunities' and 'Registration date'.
Present at the meeting and capture board decisions on next-season registration open date, calendar, and follow-ups.
Distribute the finalized recap and decisions to the board via the meeting notes doc.

title: Coordinate sponsor / donor recognition materials
details:
Support sponsor thank-you and donor management (plaques, banners, framed jerseys) with the president and sponsorship coordinator.

{{leagueAbbrev}} recognizes team sponsors and major donors with plaques, field banners, and framed jerseys, coordinated with the president and sponsorship coordinator. The information officer reviews plaque proofs from the photographer, corrects sponsor names, and organizes distribution. This work happens in the off-season so materials are ready to hand out and hang before the next season starts.
steps: Collect the finalized sponsor/team list from the sponsorship coordinator and confirm spellings and business names.
Request plaque layout proofs from the photographer (Tsukroff Photo) and review each for errors (e.g., correct 'Edson Builders' not 'Ebson').
Approve corrected proofs and send them into production, following up if the photographer is backed up during school-photo season.
Coordinate with board volunteers to pass out plaques and hang NG and {{townA}} Little League sponsor banners, ideally all in one week.
Track which sponsors have received their recognition and flag any missing framed jerseys or banners to the president.

title: Send registration-open blast and run signup nights
details:
Email the season-open registration announcement to the full league and run/promote open registration nights; start tracking division signup counts.

In early January the information officer emails the full league to announce that spring registration is open for all divisions from Tee Ball (4-6) through Seniors, along with winter clinics, Challenger, and Sandlot options. This kicks off the enrollment window, drives families to the registration portal, and starts division-level signup tracking. Getting the blast out early gives time to fill rosters and plan indoor March practices.
steps: Draft the season-open announcement (subject like '{{leagueAbbrev}} - Registration Open for the 2026 Spring Season') summarizing divisions, winter clinics, Challenger, and Sandlot.
Include the registration portal link ({{infoWebsite}}/register-practices-assessments) and the embedded season calendar with assessment dates.
Send to the full league through the registration system, timed for early January ('Happy New Year' send around 1/15-1/17).
Promote and staff any in-person open signup nights and answer inbound questions to {{infoEmail}}.
Begin tracking signups by division as registrations come in for later reporting to the board.

title: Publish finalized season calendar and key dates
details: Alongside the registration blast, the information officer publishes the finalized season calendar so families can plan around registration, clinics, assessments, draft, season start, photos, playoffs, and All-Stars. The calendar is embedded in the registration email and posted to the website's calendar page (which syncs to a public Google Calendar). Clear key dates reduce inbound questions and no-shows for assessments.
steps: Assemble the confirmed key dates: registration open, winter clinics, assessments (with gym location and age time slots), draft, season start, picture days, playoffs, and All-Stars.
Embed the '2026 Calendar' block in the registration-open email with assessment dates and rain dates (e.g., Baseball Mon 2/23, Softball Wed 2/25, rain date Fri 2/27).
Update the website calendar page ({{infoWebsite}}/home/calendar) and the subscribable {{leagueAbbrev}} Google Calendar.
Link the Little League age-chart determination tool so families confirm league age before assessments.
Re-send or update the 'Important Dates' notice if any date shifts before the season.

title: Update information website and registration portal
details: Before the season opens, the information officer refreshes the info website so division pages, the calendar, URLs, and registration-portal links all reflect the new season. This ensures families reach the correct current-year forms and info from the registration blast. It is a prerequisite for the registration announcement to work cleanly.
steps: Review each division page (Tee Ball through Seniors, plus Challenger and Sandlot) and update descriptions, ages, and season details.
Refresh the Register, Practices & Assessments pages and confirm new-registration and returning-registration flows point to the current season.
Update the calendar page and verify all internal URLs and the registration-portal link ({{infoWebsite}}) resolve correctly.
Update the certified-volunteer and FAQ pages for the new year, including annual requirements and age charts.
Do a final click-through of every link that will appear in the registration-open email before sending.

title: Send Certified Volunteer Process email to all users
details:
Blast all registered users the annual certified-volunteer process (register, background check, Abuse Awareness Training) with badge pickup instructions.

Ahead of March practices, the information officer blasts all registered users the annual certified-volunteer process so every adult on the field or in the snack shack is cleared. The email walks through the three steps (register, background check via JDP, and Abuse Awareness Training tied to {{communities}} LL) and explains league-issued badge pickup. This is a hard safety and insurance requirement, so it must land before practices begin.
steps: Send the certified-volunteer email to all registered users (subject like '{{leagueAbbrev}} - Certified Volunteer Process - 2026 Season'), timed before the March 10 practice start.
Lay out the three steps: register through {{infoWebsite}}, complete the JDP/JD Palatine background check, and take Abuse Awareness Training selecting '{{communities}} LL'.
Note the training must be redone yearly even if completed elsewhere, and link the volunteering FAQ.
Explain badge pickup: badges are issued as completions post on the certification tracker and brought to {{indoorVenue}} at 5:30 on practice days.
Send follow-up/badge reminders as practices start and games begin (e.g., pick up badges at the Douglas Field snack shack), directing name-list issues to {{secretaryEmail}}.

title: Report division signup counts to board
details:
Prepare and present division-by-division registration counts as registration nears close.

As the registration window nears close, the information officer prepares division-by-division signup counts and presents them to the board. This lets the board gauge roster viability per division, plan drafts and team counts, and push roster-fill emails where numbers are low. It typically lands just before or around assessment week.
steps: Pull current registration counts from the portal, broken out by division and by sport.
Compare against prior-year counts and minimum team thresholds to flag under-enrolled divisions.
Summarize the counts for the board meeting or email ahead of the draft.
Recommend targeted roster-fill pushes or extended registration for any short divisions.
Note players still needing assessments so the player agent can plan accordingly.

title: Prepare assessment tally and rankings for draft
details:
Compile assessment results and adjust rankings for the player agent and president ahead of the drafts.

After assessments (held at the {{indoorVenue}} gym for ages 7+ by age band), the information officer compiles the scoring results and adjusts player rankings for the player agent and president ahead of the drafts. Accurate, organized rankings make the draft fair and efficient. This is time-sensitive since assessments and the draft fall within a tight window.
steps: Collect the raw assessment scores from evaluators for each age band (7-8, 9-10, 11-12) for baseball and softball.
Aggregate scores into a ranking tally per division, accounting for late assessments and rain-date make-ups.
Reconcile the ranked list against the registered-player roster to catch missing or duplicate entries.
Adjust rankings for known factors (playing-up requests, siblings) with the player agent and president.
Deliver the finalized tally and rankings to the player agent and president before draft night.

title: Schedule Photo Day with photographer
details:
Lock picture/photo day dates with the photographer, tied to uniform delivery, and set makeup/backup dates.

The information officer locks picture day dates with Tsukroff Photo, coordinated so uniforms have arrived and teams can attend in uniform. {{leagueAbbrev}} typically runs two picture nights to work around games and practices, with per-team time slots and multiple stations. Setting makeup/backup dates up front avoids scrambling for teams that miss.
steps: Confirm uniform delivery timing, then propose picture dates to Tsukroff Photo (e.g., two nights like Mon 5/19 and Tue 5/20).
Reserve the venue (e.g., Russell Elementary Gym) and plan multiple photo stations to keep 10-15 minute team slots on schedule.
Build the per-team time-slot schedule spanning divisions and both nights, and set a makeup/backup date.
Send the picture-night announcement asking players to attend in team uniform and arrive 15 minutes early to fill out order forms.
Confirm the photographer's order/pricing options (on-site packages or online direct-order portal) and distribution plan through head coaches.

title: Report final registration and player counts
details: Once rosters are finalized after the draft, the information officer delivers final total player counts by division to the board. These numbers confirm team sizes, drive uniform and equipment orders, and set the baseline for the season. It is the definitive headcount the board plans the season around.
steps: Pull final rostered-player counts by division and sport from the registration system after the draft.
Reconcile against draft results and any late adds/drops to ensure totals match team rosters.
Compute total league player count and per-division breakdown.
Report the finalized counts to the board and share with uniform and equipment coordinators for ordering.
Archive the final counts for the season recap and year-over-year comparison.

title: Coordinate makeup team photos
details:
Work with the photographer to schedule photo sessions for teams that still need photos during their remaining games.

For teams that missed the scheduled picture nights, the information officer works with the photographer to fit makeup sessions into their remaining game schedule. This ensures every team gets a team photo for sponsor plaques and family orders. It happens mid-season after the main picture days.
steps: Identify teams and players who missed the scheduled picture nights.
Coordinate with Tsukroff Photo on available makeup dates/times, tying them to the teams' remaining home games.
Notify affected coaches and families of the makeup photo date, time, and uniform requirement.
Confirm the makeup shots include any teams still owed sponsor-plaque photos.
Track completion so no team is left without a photo for plaques or orders.

links.label: Team Photos for Sponsor Plaques template

title: Send photo packet pickup / order reminder
details:
Remind families of photo packet pickup locations and the online order deadline for the season's photos.

Late in the season the information officer reminds families where to pick up their photo packets and the deadline to order online. Packets are sorted by team at the Douglas Field snack shack, and ordering is direct through Tsukroff's online portal with prints shipped to families. A clear last-chance order date prevents missed orders.
steps: Confirm packet pickup location and hours (e.g., Douglass Field snack shack, teams present 5:30-7:30pm) with packets sorted by team.
Confirm the online order portal link and the final order deadline (e.g., last chance June 20).
Send the reminder to affected divisions clarifying online direct-order and shipping-to-home process.
Call out any correction to dates printed on the packets (e.g., 'ignore the June 5th date on the packet').
Field family questions on missing packets or orders and route to the photographer as needed.

title: Announce merch / fanwear store opening
details:
Send the merch/fanwear store-open announcement with the store link and pickup/pre-order lead-time notes.

The information officer announces the merch/fanwear store opening with the store link and pickup or pre-order lead-time notes. Because items are often produced to order, the announcement sets expectations (e.g., pickup-only, 2-3 week pre-order lead time for hats). This drives fanwear sales and supports league fundraising.
steps: Confirm the store is configured correctly (pickup-only where needed) and item availability with the sponsorship/merch coordinators.
Draft the store-open announcement (subject like '{{leagueAbbrev}} Merch Store is Open!') with the store link.
State pickup vs. pre-order terms clearly, including lead time (e.g., 'pre-order, 2-3 weeks until available' for hats).
Note any additional offerings on hand (e.g., 'Still Just a Team From {{state}}' shirts) once supply counts are confirmed.
Send the blast to the league and monitor incoming orders.

title: Organize ballpark family outings
details:
Plan and announce major- and minor-league ballpark family outings for league families.

The information officer plans and announces family experience outings to major- and minor-league ballpark games. These outings reserve a ticket block for league families, usually return a share of each ticket to the league, and sometimes tie into special on-field recognitions (e.g., honoring a state-champ All-Star team). They build community and are typically promoted in late summer.
steps: Contact the ballpark group-sales office to reserve a ticket block and group purchase link for a chosen game date.
Confirm any special on-field recognition (e.g., honoring a state-champ All-Star team) and any event sponsor.
Draft the announcement with game date/time, ticket link, and the purchase cutoff, noting when the block is released.
Include ticketing terms (refund policy, digital/QR entry) so families aren't surprised.
Send to the league and to board members where a separate board-only block exists, then remind before the deadline.

title: Wind down merch site and process refunds
details:
Close out the merch/hat store for the year and process any pending refunds.

At the end of the merch cycle the information officer closes out the fanwear/hat store for the year and processes any pending refunds. This reconciles orders that couldn't be fulfilled and cleanly ends the season's online sales. It coordinates with the treasurer and sponsorship coordinator on supply counts and payments.
steps: Confirm all pre-orders and pickups are fulfilled and reconcile against store order notifications.
Identify any unfulfilled or duplicate orders that require refunds.
Process refunds through the store/payment platform and notify affected families.
Close/disable the merch and hat store for the year and remove or archive the store link.
Coordinate final supply counts and reconciliation with the sponsorship coordinator and treasurer.

title: Present post-season survey results by division
details:
Compile and present post-season survey results and season discussion by division at year-end.

At year-end the information officer compiles and presents the post-season survey results broken out by division, leading a season discussion with the board. Division-level breakdowns surface which programs need attention (e.g., Tee Ball vs. Majors) and inform next-year structure. This closes the feedback loop that began with the survey blast earlier in the cycle.
steps: Segment the compiled survey responses by division and pull out recurring themes per division.
Summarize positives, negatives, and complaints for each division into a concise board-ready format.
Add the by-division results to the year-end board meeting agenda for discussion.
Lead the season discussion, capturing decisions and action items per division.
Record outcomes in the meeting notes to carry into next season's planning.

title: Facilitate fall organizational meeting and confirm officer slate
details:
Run the fall organizational board meeting, designate facilitator/recorder, take attendance/quorum, and carry the motion to fill and approve the officer slate for the coming year.

The fall organizational meeting kicks off the league year, resetting the Board of Directors and confirming who holds each voting officer and non-voting staff role for the coming season. It matters because officers must be in place before offseason planning (calendar, budget, sponsorship) can proceed, and because the elected slate is recorded in the minutes that the league keeps on file. Held in late September/early October (e.g., the 9/29 kickoff meeting), it is the first meeting after the season wraps.
steps: Before the meeting, survey members on which roles they will not continue in so open seats (e.g., Treasurer, Player Agents, VP Softball) can be listed and recruited.
Designate a facilitator and recorder (the President typically serves both) and open the meeting by taking attendance and confirming a quorum.
Walk the full positions list, noting which roles are retained and which are marked open or '??'.
For each seat to be filled, take a named motion and second, then record the vote outcome ('carried unanimously/unopposed') in the minutes.
Create any new positions needed (e.g., VP Sandlot, VP Challenger) by separate motion, then elect a person to fill them.
Publish the confirmed slate and note remaining open seats to carry into recruiting at the next meeting.

title: Establish offseason board meeting schedule
details:
Set the fall/winter meeting cadence (monthly or bi-weekly) and circulate the schedule to the board.

Setting the fall/winter meeting cadence gives the Board a predictable rhythm for offseason planning, which shifts to roughly every two weeks during the busy pre-season period and monthly in quieter stretches. It matters because registration, clinics, assessments, and calendar decisions all depend on a reliable sequence of meetings. This is settled at or immediately after the fall organizational meeting.
steps: Decide the appropriate cadence for the period (bi-weekly through pre-season, monthly otherwise) to maximize program quality.
Poll board members for dates/times that work best rather than dictating them.
Lock the fall/winter meeting dates (e.g., the recurring bi-weekly Monday evening pattern seen Oct through Dec).
Circulate the confirmed schedule to the full board and add it to the shared calendar.
Note the standard join method (in-person location or video/dial-in) so it can be reused in each meeting announcement.

title: Lead annual policy and division rules review
details:
Review and adopt division rules, the managers/coaches contract, and the volunteer application; confirm bylaws obligations with the secretary.

Each fall/winter the Board reviews and adopts the season's governing documents: division rules, the managers/coaches contract, the volunteer application, and the Constitution & By-laws. This matters because the bylaws must be reviewed, updated, and uploaded to Little League International as a recurring charter obligation, and division rules (age structure, play-up, farm/coach-pitch changes) shape the whole season. The review runs across the fall meetings before registration opens.
steps: Put policy review on the agenda: division rules, managers/coaches contract, volunteer application, and bylaws.
Review and adopt division age/level structure and any interleague rule changes by division, poll the league where needed.
Confirm with the Secretary that the Constitution & By-laws are current and uploaded to Little League International.
Adopt each change by motion and second, recording the outcome in the minutes.
Confirm Abuse Awareness Training (resets October 1) is required of all board members and track completion.
Publish the finalized rules/documents to the website and Policies & Procedures page.

title: Kick off next-season planning
details: This task drafts the skeleton of the coming season -- registration timing, winter clinics, assessments, the full calendar, and coaches trainings -- for board input and refinement. It matters because these anchor dates drive every downstream officer's work, from uniform orders to field scheduling. It happens in the fall (late October/November) so the calendar can be finalized before registration opens in January.
steps: Draft proposed dates for registration open, winter clinics, assessments, coaches clinics, drafts, and first games.
Assemble prospective clinic costs and instructors and confirm facility availability with contacts.
Present the draft calendar to the board for discussion and adjust based on school-calendar conflicts and facility bookings.
Fold in coaches-training plans (e.g., the PCA coach/parent/athlete workshop series) and safety-meeting requirements.
Circulate the revised draft calendar ahead of the next meeting for a final review.

title: Coordinate sponsor thank-yous and fundraising follow-up
details:
Organize sponsor thank-yous (banners, signed/dye-sub jerseys, donation letters) by donation tier and follow up on outstanding fundraising.

After the season the league recognizes sponsors by donation tier -- banners, signed/dye-sub jerseys, and donation letters -- and follows up on any outstanding fundraising commitments. It matters for sponsor retention and for closing out the season's revenue, since sponsorships fund uniforms, equipment, and field work. Thank-you acknowledgements are driven from the Annual Sponsorship Log in the offseason (seen in January/February).
steps: Pull the Annual Sponsorship Log and reconcile sponsors and amounts across channels (checks, PayPal, Venmo, GoFundMe).
Group sponsors by donation tier, highlighting larger donors (e.g., $250+ and $500+) for extra recognition.
Prepare tier-appropriate thank-yous: banners, signed/dye-sub jerseys, and tax-deductible donation letters.
Coordinate with the Sponsorship Coordinator and Treasurer to send acknowledgements and complete any corporate donation forms.
Follow up on outstanding pledges or unpaid team sponsorships before the uniform-order cutoff.
Update the website sponsor list and note rollovers/refunds for any unfulfilled sponsorships.

title: Set registration fees and open date
details:
Recommend and confirm registration fees by division and the registration open date with the board.

The Board sets per-division registration fees and the registration open date, which together drive the league's primary revenue and the start of the season pipeline. It matters because fees fund uniforms and field repairs and any change must be adopted by motion; the open date anchors the whole calendar. This is decided in the fall/winter (fees set by December motion; open dates targeted for mid-January).
steps: Review current-year costs and prior fees by division (e.g., 2025 moved everything AAA and above to {{amount}}).
Recommend per-division fees and earmark any increase (e.g., toward field repairs) for board consideration.
Adopt the fee schedule by motion and second, recording the outcome.
Confirm the registration open date (e.g., mid-January for regular season, early January for winter clinics).
Hand the confirmed fees and dates to the Information Officer to configure in the registration system.

title: Send fall board meeting announcement with agenda
details:
Announce the fall board meeting to the board with agenda; follow up with a reminder including the join link/dial-in.

This announces each fall board meeting to the board with the agenda, followed by a reminder that includes the join link or dial-in. It matters because consistent, agenda-forward announcements keep quorum and let officers prepare their updates. It recurs on the offseason cadence (roughly every two weeks through fall/winter).
steps: Draft the agenda from carryover action items and the standing offseason topics (positions, planning, fields, calendar).
Send the meeting announcement to the board with the date/time and agenda attached or linked.
A day or two before, send a reminder reply on the same thread including the video join link and dial-in number.
Confirm the recorder for the meeting so minutes are captured.
After the meeting, ensure minutes and updated action items are circulated.

title: Plan winter clinics
details: Winter clinics give players ages 7+ a chance to get work in before spring assessments, and the league must lock dates, gym space, age-group time slots, instructors, budget, and session fees. It matters because clinics are optional paid programming that requires facility booking and a registration listing well ahead of time. Dates are set in the fall and clinics run on winter weekends (e.g., three January/February Sunday sessions).
steps: Assemble prospective clinic costs and instructor availability and include facility costs in the budget.
Lock clinic dates and reserve the middle-school gym, tasking a board member with checking the school calendar to book spaces.
Build the age-group time-slot grid (e.g., AA / AAA / Majors baseball and softball blocks plus an all-ages pitching clinic).
Set session fees (e.g., a per-session or all-sessions bundle price) for board approval.
Coordinate with the Information Officer to open clinic registration alongside the season (early January).
Announce clinics to families with dates, slots, and the registration link.

title: Set assessment dates and structure
details:
Establish spring assessment dates, station structure, judges, and snow/rain dates.

The Board establishes spring assessment dates, the station-based structure, judges/assessors, and a snow/rain make-up date so teams can be formed by the draft. It matters because assessments are required for all players League Age 7+ and feed the coaches' draft; separate baseball and softball days and a reserved make-up date protect against weather closures. Dates are set in the fall/winter (e.g., baseball 2/23, softball 2/25, make-up 2/27).
steps: Set separate baseball and softball assessment dates plus a reserved snow/rain make-up date.
Reserve the gym for the evening blocks (e.g., 4:30-9:00pm) and confirm space against the school calendar.
Define the station structure (ground balls, fly/pop, tee, soft toss, throwing) each staffed by a coach and an assessor.
Build the time-block grid by division/age (e.g., AA 5:30, AAA 6:30, Majors 7:30).
Recruit assessors/judges and high-school player volunteers to run stations.
Confirm the draft date a few days after assessments so ratings are ready.

title: Recruit and confirm open board positions
details:
Confirm/retain roles, fill open seats, and recruit volunteers ahead of the spring season.

Ahead of spring the President confirms which roles are retained, fills open seats, and recruits volunteers for both voting and non-voting positions. It matters because operational roles (Treasurer, Player Agents, VP Softball, Concessions, uniform/photo staff) must be staffed before the season ramps up. Recruiting runs across the fall/winter meetings, with vacancies filled at the next board meeting.
steps: Review the positions list and mark each seat as retained, open, or newly created.
Announce the open positions to the board and the wider league and invite volunteers.
For key long-term seats (e.g., Treasurer), state that the holder must be a board member and set an announcement window.
Bring each candidate to a vote by motion and second at the next board meeting and record the result.
Update the published board roster and note any still-open seats to keep recruiting.

title: Broadcast registration-open announcement
details:
Send the registration-open broadcast to all families with tee ball/coach pitch details, winter clinics, and the custom-uniform sign-up deadline.

This is the league-wide broadcast to all families that registration is open, covering tee ball/coach pitch details, winter clinics, and the custom-uniform sign-up deadline. It matters because it drives enrollment across every division and sets expectations on age determination, clinics, Sandlot/Challenger, and the firm jersey deadline. It goes out when registration opens in mid-January (e.g., January 17 for 2026).
steps: Confirm the open date and per-division details, then draft the broadcast covering Tee Ball through Seniors.
Include age-determination guidance (Aug 31 baseball, Jan 1 softball) and a link to the Little League age charts.
Highlight winter clinics, Sandlot, and Challenger sign-ups and the online registration link.
State the firm custom-jersey registration deadline (e.g., 3/14, no exceptions) prominently.
Coordinate with the Information Officer to send to all families and post on the website/social channels.

title: Plan player assessments logistics
details:
Organize assessment dates, stations, assessors/judges, equipment per station, check-in flow, and a snow/rain backup date.

Beyond setting dates, this organizes the on-the-ground logistics: stations, assessors/judges, equipment per station, check-in flow, and a snow/rain backup. It matters because a smooth, well-staffed assessment produces reliable ratings for the draft and keeps parents informed. It is finalized in the weeks before assessments (late February).
steps: Lay out each station (ground balls, fly/pop, tee, soft toss, throwing) with the equipment it needs.
Assign a coach plus an assessor to each station and line up high-school player volunteers.
Design a check-in flow and time-block schedule so divisions rotate through stations by age group.
Arrange the concurrent parent meeting space (library or chorus room) for the season presentation.
Confirm the snow/rain backup date and the communication plan if a session is postponed.
Provide league helmets/bats on site and remind families to bring a change of shoes and their glove.

title: Secure indoor practice / spring training space
details:
Book gym/YMCA time and schedule indoor practices with volunteer setup coverage.

This books gym/YMCA time and schedules indoor practices with volunteer setup coverage before fields are usable. It matters because {{state}} spring weather forces early-season practices indoors, and the limited gym space must be reserved and staffed. Booking happens in the winter and indoor practices run on weekends through March/early April (e.g., Saturdays 3/8-4/12).
steps: Identify available indoor spaces (school gyms, YMCA, The Cages) and check dates against the school calendar.
Reserve the indoor blocks and build a per-division/age indoor practice schedule.
Line up volunteer setup coverage for equipment and space turnover between sessions.
Adopt any safety rules for indoor use (e.g., league bats only, no personal bats, parents out unless helping).
Announce indoor practice start to families with dates, locations, and weather caveats.

title: Lead rules and division review
details:
Review division rules and interleague rule changes (farm system, coach pitch, age structure, playing-up) with the board.

This reviews division rules and interleague rule changes with the board -- farm/coach-pitch structure, age structure, and playing-up requests -- so the season's play framework is settled. It matters because rule and age-structure decisions (e.g., phased Intermediate rules for Majors, steals/no dropped-third-strike at Minors) affect safety, competitiveness, and interleague alignment. This runs through the winter meetings before drafts.
steps: Put the level/age structure and any proposed rule changes on the agenda by division.
Review interleague rule changes and align with {{district}} expectations where applicable.
Apply the play-up rule case by case, weighing player and peer safety, assessment, and grade level.
Poll the league where a change is significant (e.g., phased Intermediate rules rollout).
Adopt each rule/structure decision by motion and second and record it.
Publish the confirmed division rules to coaches and the website.

title: Send assessments/registration reminder
details: This reminds families of assessment dates, what to bring, the parent meeting, the medical release form, and the per-division schedule grid. It matters because turnout and preparedness at assessments directly affect the quality of ratings and team formation, and late registrants can still be placed. It goes out in the week or two before assessments (mid-to-late February).
steps: Confirm the assessment dates, division time blocks, and make-up date, then draft the reminder.
Include what to bring: change of shoes, glove; note helmets/bats are optional since the league provides them.
Remind families to bring a printed medical release form if not yet submitted.
Note the concurrent parent meeting and its location and the season presentation.
Attach or embed the per-division schedule grid and send to all affected families.
If a session is postponed for weather/closure, follow up promptly with the make-up details.

title: Run coach interviews and vetting vote
details:
Invite coaches to interviews, provide instructions, and conduct the board's ranked-choice vetting vote per division.

The President invites prospective coaches to interviews, provides instructions, and conducts the board's ranked-choice vetting vote per division. It matters because coach selection sets the tone for player experience, safety, and conduct, and the ranked vote gives the board a defensible, division-by-division ordering ahead of election. It happens after assessments and before the draft (late February/early March).
steps: Compile the list of coach applicants by division and confirm they have completed required training (e.g., PCA, Abuse Awareness) and background checks.
Invite prospective coaches to interviews with clear instructions on format and timing.
Conduct interviews and gather board impressions on conduct, rules knowledge, and technique.
Run the board's ranked-choice vetting vote per division and tally the ordering.
Record the results to carry into the coach-election motions.
Keep applicant information confidential to the board.

title: Elect coaches and set team counts
details:
Bring motions to elect coaches and set the number of teams per level; review play-up/move-up requests for safety and balance.

This brings motions to elect coaches and set the number of teams per level, and reviews play-up/move-up requests for safety and balance. It matters because team counts must match registration numbers before the draft, and elected coaches and approved play-ups determine roster composition. It follows the vetting vote and precedes the draft (early March).
steps: Using the ranked vetting results and current registration counts, propose the number of teams per level.
Bring a motion to set team counts per division; second and record the outcome.
Bring motions to elect head coaches per division based on the ranked vote.
Review each play-up/move-up request against safety, assessment, and competency at the target level.
Approve or decline play-ups by motion, noting any approval may carry to future levels.
Finalize the coach and team-count list to feed the draft schedule.

title: Set draft dates and enforce jersey deadline
details:
Schedule drafts after the coaches meeting and enforce the 3/14 final custom-jersey registration deadline (no exceptions).

This schedules the division drafts after the coaches meeting and enforces the final custom-jersey registration deadline (3/14, no exceptions). It matters because the deadline lets the league finalize teams and place the uniform order on time, and the drafts must follow assessments closely so ratings are fresh. Both fall in early-to-mid March.
steps: Schedule each division's draft for the days after the coaches meeting and assessments.
Confirm ratings are set, including chosen ratings for players who missed assessments.
Communicate and enforce the 3/14 final custom-jersey registration deadline with no exceptions.
Confirm teams are finalized by the deadline so the uniform order can proceed.
Send division draft invites to head/assistant coaches with the meeting link and dial-in.
Run each division draft (roughly 30-45 minutes) among that division's head coaches.

title: Finalize season calendar
details:
Finalize clinics, assessments, coaches clinics, draft, field cleanups, first games, and All-Star letters/dates.

Lock down the full season calendar so every downstream activity has a firm date to build against. This consolidates clinics, assessments, coaches clinics, drafts, field cleanups, first-game dates, and the All-Star letter/deadline dates into one authoritative reference. It matters because uniform ordering, scheduling, and family communications all key off these dates, and drafts in particular must land before uniform-order cutoffs.
steps: Gather draft dates from the prior year's calendar and confirm gym/field availability and any Little League deadlines.
Sequence winter clinics, assessments, and coaches clinics ahead of the drafts for each division.
Set division draft dates so they complete before the uniform-order cutoff (drafts historically finalized by late March).
Add field cleanup/workdays, first-game targets, and the All-Star Letter-of-Intent due date (early-to-mid May in recent seasons).
Circulate the draft calendar to the board for review and adjust for conflicts.
Publish the finalized calendar to the website and reference it in registration and clinic communications.

title: Send division draft invites
details:
Invite head/assistant coaches to each division draft, propose evenings, share coach lists, and include the online meeting link and dial-in.

Invite each division's head and assistant coaches to their draft and set the meeting. This kicks off team formation for the season and must be timed so all divisions draft before the uniform-order cutoff. The invite establishes the roster of participating coaches, proposes evenings, and shares the online meeting details so remote coaches can attend.
steps: Email the confirmed head/assistant coach list for the division and note any coaches still needed (e.g., aiming for 6 teams at AAA for scheduling and playing time).
Propose evening dates and confirm the final date, allowing slack to recruit an additional coach if a division is short.
Explain the snake-order draft mechanics (1-6, 6-1) and coach's-kid/assistant-coach rules so coaches arrive prepared.
Include the Google Meet video link and any dial-in for coaches attending remotely.
Attach the draft sheet/info and flag any special cases (e.g., an all-town team highlighted for skipping).
Send a same-day reminder with the meeting link before the draft (drafts have run at 7:30pm).

title: Release draft results and collect team names
details: After each division drafts, publish the per-team rosters and practice schedules to coaches, then collect each team's ranked team-name choices. This lets coaches introduce themselves and begin scheduling, and the ranked choices with a coin-flip tiebreaker prevent duplicate team names across the division. It occurs immediately after the draft and before rosters are entered into GameChanger.
steps: Evaluate drafted teams for age, average-score, and overall balance and process any equitable trades before finalizing.
Send each coach their team roster and the initial practice schedule.
Ask coaches to reach out to their teams to introduce themselves and begin scheduling practices.
Collect ranked team-name choices from each coach and resolve duplicate requests using a coin-flip tiebreaker.
Confirm the final team names back to coaches so they can be entered into GameChanger.

links.label: Draft results and team names template

title: Ensure rosters published to GameChanger
details:
Direct the secretary to enter drafted teams into GameChanger and post rosters.

Direct the secretary to enter each drafted team into GameChanger and confirm the rosters are posted so families and coaches can view teams and schedules. GameChanger is the league's official app for rosters, schedules, and coach-family communication, so this is a prerequisite for practices and games. Import issues are common, so plan for follow-up and re-posting.
steps: Direct the secretary to enter each finalized team and roster into GameChanger.
Confirm each team imports correctly, retrying if teams fail to import or spin during setup.
Announce to families that rosters are posted and that their login matches their {{registrationPlatform}}/registration login.
Share the GameChanger FAQ link for families who have not used the app ({{infoWebsite}}/frequently-asked-questions/game-changer).
Note that families may need to reload their team if they hit earlier import issues, and invite questions.

title: Announce optional pre-season practices
details:
Announce optional pre-season/outdoor practices to families with the GameChanger app link, FAQ, and weather caveats.

Announce optional outdoor pre-season practices to families so teams can get on the field before games begin without losing good-weather days. Coaches post specific times and fields to GameChanger, so the announcement points families there and sets weather expectations. It runs in the weeks after drafts and before the regular season opens.
steps: Confirm which divisions will hold optional outdoor practices and which fields are available.
Tell families coaches will add practice times and fields to GameChanger and to check there for assignments.
Direct families to download the GameChanger app and sign in with their registration login (https://www.gc.com), and share the FAQ for finding their team.
Set expectations that practices are optional and weather-dependent, and to bundle up for cool early-season conditions.
Note any divisions still being worked out so families know more may follow.

title: Distribute {{district}} and All-Star tournament info
details: Share {{district}} updates, interleague forms, and All-Star tournament dates with the board and coaches so the league can plan for tournament and interleague play. This keeps the board aligned on district deadlines and gives coaches early visibility into the All-Star timeline. It happens in-season as {{district}} finalizes schedules and affidavit/eligibility requirements.
steps: Collect current {{district}} updates, interleague forms, and All-Star tournament dates from the district administrator.
Summarize the relevant deadlines (commitment/letter-of-intent, affidavit signing, tournament brackets) for the board.
Distribute the info and any required interleague forms to the board and affected coaches.
Point families and coaches to the All-Stars/Tournaments FAQ for eligibility and scheduling details.
Track district deadlines that require league action (rosters, affidavits) and assign owners.

title: Broadcast season schedules update
details: Send families a season-opening schedule status by division, directing them to GameChanger for the authoritative schedule. This manages expectations when the scheduling system is still being finalized and tells each division when practices and games start. It is sent as the regular season opens, often while the scheduling provider is still resolving sync issues.
steps: Confirm the current status of the scheduling system and each division's practice/game start dates.
Give a per-division breakdown of what is posted versus pending (e.g., tee ball/coach pitch start weeks, AA/AAA/Majors practice and game starts).
Explain that coaches will enter upcoming practices in GameChanger until full schedules are posted.
Direct all families to GameChanger for their schedule and note when full schedules are expected.
Send the update to all families across divisions and invite questions.

title: Coordinate Snack Shack setup and staffing
details: Coordinate opening the Snack Shack and recruiting volunteer staffing (baseball and softball) so concessions are ready when games start. Concessions are a key league fundraiser and require setup plus a steady rotation of volunteers. This is done right before the season's first games and repeated for softball opening day.
steps: Confirm the Snack Shack is stocked, cleaned, and set up ahead of the first games.
Recruit or confirm a concessions/Snack Shack manager to run day-to-day operations.
Post volunteer sign-ups for opening day and early game dates, including a separate softball opening-day slot.
Coordinate field maintenance and setup alongside concessions where they overlap.
Follow up on unfilled shifts and remind families that help keeps the Snack Shack open.

links.label: Snack Shack volunteers - opening day template

title: Broadcast field etiquette and start times
details: Send families field rules, start times, arrival windows, and neighbor-respect reminders to keep events safe and on good terms with shared facilities. This became critical when weekday events at fields overlapped with other town programs and a safety incident occurred in a pickup line. It is sent early in the game season and reissued whenever start times or arrival windows change.
steps: Identify overlaps between league events and other programs at shared fields (e.g., town rec pickup lines).
Set adjusted start times and a no-early-arrival window to reduce congestion (e.g., events start at 6pm, no arrival before 5:30pm).
Publish warm-up and game start windows per division so families know when to arrive.
Explain the safety rationale and stress respecting neighbors and shared-facility partners.
Send to all affected families and repeat if start times or arrival rules change.

links.label: Field etiquette and start times template

title: Manage All-Star commitment intake
details:
Collect All-Star commitment forms by the deadline; require a full 14-player slate for a nomination to be accepted.

Collect All-Star commitment (Letter of Intent) forms by the deadline and verify each division has a full 14-player slate before accepting a nomination. Without a submitted form a player cannot be considered for tournament play, so intake determines which teams can even be fielded. The deadline runs early-to-mid May, historically due by 11:59pm on a set date.
steps: Publish the online Letter-of-Intent/commitment form with the deadline (recent seasons due ~May 18-19 at 11:59pm).
Direct families to the All-Stars FAQ for eligibility and to route questions to their manager or the secretary.
Include the school-residency permission option so the district can verify enrollment in bulk.
Send a reminder before the deadline and consolidate all submissions (including earlier paper forms) in one place.
Tally commitments by division/level and confirm a full 14-player slate before accepting a nomination.
Flag any division short of 14 for a team-not-fielded decision.

title: Schedule playoffs and end-of-season events
details: Build the playoff brackets and plan the end-of-season celebration (championship-day BBQ and Home Run Derby) with volunteers. Playoffs run the first two weeks of June with double-elimination brackets and consolation games, and championship day features a free BBQ. This work sets the competitive close of the season and the community celebration around it.
steps: Draw first-round matchups by random draw and update schedules so the last set-opponent game is the first playoff game.
Publish double-elimination brackets online and note placeholders for unknown later-round matchups.
Set home-team rules (first round by coin flip, later rounds by playoff winning percentage) and rainout/make-up plans.
Include consolation-game guidance so eliminated teams end on a fun note (medals, treats, Banana Ball).
Plan the championship-day BBQ (free burgers/hot dogs/chips/drinks starting ~11am) and recruit grill and Snack Shack volunteers.
Coordinate a Home Run Derby with age-tiered stations and sign-ups if running the event.

title: Run All-Star team and coach selection
details: Conduct the All-Star roster votes by division/level and elect head and assistant coaches, pending background checks. This determines which players and coaches represent the league in tournament play and must follow the league's voting and eligibility rules. It runs after commitment intake closes and full slates are confirmed.
steps: Confirm the eligible player pool per division/level from committed Letters of Intent.
Run the roster vote for each division/level following league voting procedures.
Elect a head coach and assistant coaches for each team, contingent on background checks.
Confirm all selected coaches have current, cleared background checks before announcing.
Notify elected head coaches and have them finalize their coaching staff (e.g., naming a third coach).
Prepare finalized rosters for board approval.

title: Obtain board approval of All-Star rosters
details: Present the finalized All-Star rosters per division for formal board approval, then notify coaches.
