Board approval is the governance checkpoint that authorizes the teams to represent the league in tournament play. It follows selection and precedes setting up teams in GameChanger and scheduling practices.
steps: Compile the finalized roster for each division/level from the completed selection votes.
Present the rosters to the board and obtain a recorded approval motion.
Confirm all coaches on approved teams have cleared background checks.
Notify head coaches of approval and set up each team in GameChanger.
Announce the head coach and roster to families and enable practice scheduling.

title: Send team-not-fielded notices
details: Notify affected families when a division lacks enough commitments to field an All-Star team. A full 14-player slate is required, and when a division falls short the league cannot nominate a team, so families need a clear, timely explanation. This is sent once commitment tallies confirm a shortfall.
steps: Confirm the division's committed count is below the required 14-player slate.
Draft a clear notice explaining the team cannot be fielded and why the minimum matters.
Offer any alternatives where applicable (combined/interleague options or fall/other play).
Send the notice to affected families in that division and thank them for committing.
Update the board and district on which teams will and will not be fielded.

title: Send coach conduct reminders
details: Send game-conduct reminders to coaches during summer/All-Star ball and follow up promptly on any parent complaint. Maintaining positive sideline and dugout behavior protects players, volunteers, and the league's standing, especially in higher-stakes tournament play. This runs through the summer season and is triggered again whenever a conduct concern is reported.
steps: Send a periodic game-conduct reminder to coaches emphasizing positivity toward kids, umpires, and volunteers.
Reinforce dugout safety expectations and uniform enforcement of team behavior rules.
When a complaint arrives, acknowledge it promptly and gather firsthand accounts from involved coaches/volunteers.
Follow up with the coach and, where needed, the parents to resolve the issue and restore a safe environment.
Escalate to the board and document if behavior does not improve after warnings.

title: Facilitate post-season business meeting
details: Run the post-season board meeting to review the season survey, confirm fall ball counts, plan the banquet/parade and awards/rings, and schedule board elections. This is the league's transition meeting from the current season into the offseason and next-year planning. It sets the agenda for wrap-up work and leadership continuity.
steps: Announce the meeting date and circulate an agenda covering survey review, fall ball, banquet/parade, awards/rings, and elections.
Review the end-of-season survey results and pull out actionable feedback.
Confirm fall ball counts and any interleague/{{district}} fall commitments.
Plan the banquet/parade and decide on awards and championship rings with owners and budget.
Schedule board elections and identify open positions and candidates.
Assign end-of-season to-do items (concessions cleanout, gear bins, field maintenance) and record decisions in the minutes.

title: Draft following-year calendar
details: Draft the following year's calendar (registration, clinics, assessments, coaches clinics, season dates, and All-Stars) for board review. Building the calendar in the offseason gives the board time to align on dates before registration opens and lets all downstream planning key off firm dates. This is a year-end planning task that seeds the next season's operations.
steps: Start from the current year's calendar and note what worked or needs to shift.
Set registration open/close dates and the winter clinic and assessment schedule.
Place coaches clinics and division draft dates ahead of the uniform-order cutoff.
Set season start dates, opening day, and playoff/championship targets.
Add the All-Star Letter-of-Intent deadline and tournament windows.
Circulate the draft calendar for board review and revise before publishing.

title: Review ASAP safety plan and audit AED devices
details:
Refresh the ASAP (As Safe As Possible) plan for the new year and inspect every AED device (battery, pads, location). Report status to the board.

Refresh {{leagueAbbrev}}'s written As Safe As Possible (ASAP) plan for the new charter year and inventory every AED so the league starts the season compliant with Little League's Child Protection and safety requirements. Most years this is a simple update of officer positions, emergency numbers, and field/facility details on the existing plan, plus confirming each donated AED (e.g., the Reliance Matrix units placed at league-owned fields like Pennell/Douglas) is present with a working battery and in-date pads. Doing it early lets the plan be submitted by the District's spring deadline and reported to the board.
steps: Pull last year's ASAP plan (maintained as a shared Google Doc) and update officer names, contact numbers, and field/emergency information.
Locate each league AED, check the battery and pad expiration, confirm it is at its assigned snack shack/field, and note any that need service or replacement.
Confirm first aid kits and safety signage are accounted for so gaps can be ordered before games.
Add a safety/AED status item to the next board meeting agenda and report findings to the board.
Submit the finalized ASAP plan to {{state}} {{district}} / Little League ahead of the spring deadline (District has historically targeted a late-March due date).

links.label: Equipment, Uniforms & Safety policy (Safety Program / ASAP)

title: Track fall Abuse Awareness training completions
details: After Little League's October 1 reset, collect the annual Abuse Awareness Training certificates from all board members and volunteers and update the certification tracking list. Little League International requires the course be re-completed every year (District Administrators had a December 1 deadline, with reminder notices escalating to a final notice), so early tracking prevents last-minute scrambles. Keeping the tracker current feeds directly into who can be badged as a Certified Volunteer in the spring.
steps: Confirm the Abuse Awareness course has reset for the new year and share the Little League University course link with board members and volunteers.
As certificates arrive, record each completion in the league's certification tracking system.
Cross-check that board members and returning coaches have re-completed for the current year, since prior-year completions do not carry over.
Send escalating reminders to anyone outstanding ahead of the December 1 Little League deadline.
Report completion status to the board and flag anyone who cannot yet be certified.

title: Schedule coaches clinic and LL Safety & First Aid training
details: Book the venue, date, and instructor for the mandatory Little League Safety & First Aid training and the coaches clinic, then announce to coaches with a signup goal. {{leagueAbbrev}} runs this as a Coaches Safety Meeting & Training Session covering the safety manual, rules, and coaching tips, typically split into an AA/AAA/Majors session and a Tee Ball/Coach Pitch session at the {{indoorVenue}} cafeteria in March. Every team must have at least one coach attend to meet Little League safety requirements, so scheduling before the season and pushing attendance is essential.
steps: Reserve the {{indoorVenue}} cafeteria and set two evening sessions (one for AA/AAA/Majors, one for Tee Ball/Coach Pitch), historically 6-8pm on weeknights in mid-March.
Confirm the safety agenda: safety manual/ASAP review, rules discussion, and a coach training Q&A; note Little League also now requires the online Safety Awareness and First Aid Awareness courses.
Announce dates to all coaches, stressing that each team must have at least one coach attend to meet Little League requirements.
Track RSVPs against a per-team attendance goal and send a same-day reminder before each session.
Record attendance and follow up with any team that did not have a coach present.

title: Organize subsidized AED/CPR (Heartsaver) clinic
details: Arrange and subsidize a CPR/AED Heartsaver clinic for coaches and volunteers, confirming the instructor, materials, and registration. {{leagueAbbrev}} has sponsored a discounted class (covering half of the ~$50 fee, so ~$25 per participant) at the {{indoorVenue}} cafeteria, covering CPR, the Heimlich maneuver, EPI pens/medications, and AED use to pair trained responders with the league's AED devices. Because turnout can be low and sessions sometimes need rescheduling, confirm a viable headcount before committing the instructor.
steps: Confirm the instructor and a spring evening date/time at the {{indoorVenue}} cafeteria (past sessions ran ~3-4 hours, roughly 5:30-9:30pm).
Set the subsidized price (league covers about half; participants historically paid ~{{amount}}) and open a registration form (Google Form) with a signup link.
Announce the discounted clinic to parents, coaches, and volunteers and note the curriculum: CPR, Heimlich, EPI pens/medication, and AED devices.
Verify enrollment is high enough to be worth the instructor's time before finalizing; reschedule as one block if needed.
Track completions in the certification records and reimburse or pay the instructor promptly after the class.

title: Verify certified-volunteer badges before practices start
details: Cross-check background checks and Abuse Awareness completions so every on-field volunteer is a Certified Volunteer with a league-issued badge before practices begin. {{leagueAbbrev}} requires anyone in the snack shack, on the field when children are present, or at practice facilities to wear their badge; a record is badge-eligible only when it shows "Passed" verification status and a "Y"/"M" for Abuse Awareness completed. Because indoor practices start in March, badges must be ready to hand out at {{indoorVenue}} (5:30 on practice days) so approved coaches and helpers can run practices.
steps: Confirm each volunteer completed all three steps: registration, JDP background check, and Abuse Awareness (plus the newer Safety and First Aid Awareness courses).
In the certification tracking system, treat a volunteer as certified only when verification shows "Passed" and Abuse Awareness shows "Y" or "M".
Print/assemble badges and lanyards for all completed volunteers.
Bring badges to {{indoorVenue}} at 5:30 on practice days (and later to a snack shack such as Douglas Field on game days) for pickup and notify volunteers when theirs is ready.
Follow up with anyone still missing a step so they are cleared before their team's practices begin.

title: Distribute ASAP plan packets to all coaches
details: Provide each coach a copy of the ASAP plan plus completed medical release forms for their players to carry to all games and practices. {{leagueAbbrev}} assembles these as ASAP/medical release binders distributed at the coaches safety meeting or with the season equipment (books, balls, forms), and coaches who did not receive a copy are told to contact {{infoEmail}}. A Medical Release Form must be completed annually for every player, so this pairs the safety plan with current player medical info in one packet.
steps: Print current ASAP plan copies and confirm a completed, in-year Medical Release Form exists for every rostered player.
Assemble per-team binders/packets pairing the ASAP plan with that team's medical release forms.
Distribute packets at the coaches safety meeting or alongside season equipment distribution (ASAP books, balls, forms).
Remind coaches they must carry the ASAP plan and medical releases to all games and practices.
Direct any coach missing a copy to email {{infoEmail}} and backfill missing medical releases.

title: Install safety bases at all fields
details: Install break-away safety bases at every field before the first games and verify each field is game-ready, noting any equipment needs. {{leagueAbbrev}} has tracked this as a spring pre-season action ("Safety Base Install - will install before games begin") and revisits base condition during end-of-season field work at all fields. Break-away bases reduce sliding injuries, so completing the install before opening games is a safety compliance step tied to field readiness.
steps: Inventory break-away safety base sets for every field and identify any missing or worn bases to reorder.
Coordinate with the grounds crew to install/anchor safety bases at each field before the first scheduled games.
Walk each field to confirm bases, anchors, and mounds are game-ready and safe.
Log any equipment needs or field hazards and route repairs to the appropriate coordinator.
Confirm completion to the board so opening games are cleared to proceed.

title: File injury and concussion incident reports
details: Complete incident reports for any injuries, and especially concussions, for the league insurer, and enforce the physician-cleared return-to-play protocol with parents and coaches. Coaches report incidents (e.g., a player struck by a softball) to the Safety Officer and president, who documents details and follows up on the player's care. The Safety Officer files reports as injuries occur and, for concussions, ensures the player does not return to play until cleared in writing by a physician.
steps: Collect the incident details from the reporting coach: player, date, field, what happened, and any care provided.
Complete the Little League/insurer injury report and retain a copy in league records.
For any head injury/concussion, require written physician clearance before the player returns to any practice or game.
Communicate the return-to-play protocol to the player's parents and the coach and confirm they understand it.
Follow up on the player's status and close out the report; escalate to the president/District as needed.

title: Confirm AED coverage for All-Star and summer teams
details: Ensure AED devices, first aid kits, and current safety documentation travel with All-Star and summer/tournament teams, which play away games against other {{district}} towns (Westbrook, Portland, Scarborough, Cape Elizabeth, etc.) from mid-July into August. Because these teams frequently play off league-owned fields, portable safety coverage and up-to-date medical releases must go with them. Confirming this before summer play begins keeps the league compliant when kids are away from the home fields' fixed AEDs.
steps: Identify each All-Star and summer team's schedule and which games are away from league-owned fields.
Assign a portable AED and stocked first aid kit to travel with each team, checking battery/pad dates and restocking kits.
Confirm each team carries current safety documentation and completed player medical release forms.
Verify All-Star and summer coaches/volunteers are certified (background check + Abuse Awareness) and badged.
Confirm coverage to the board/coaches before the summer season opens (typically mid-July).

title: Update ASAP plan for post-season and tournament play
details: Revise the ASAP/SAFE plan for post-season, All-Star, and tournament activity and confirm all participating teams have current safety compliance. Tournament play adds new venues, later-summer conditions, and District/Little League requirements (including that any player-absence tournament forms be completed by the parent), so the safety plan and volunteer certifications must be re-verified. This keeps {{leagueAbbrev}}'s post-season teams compliant with {{state}} {{district}} and Little League tournament rules.
steps: Review the ASAP/SAFE plan and update it for tournament venues, emergency contacts, and summer conditions.
Re-verify that all tournament coaches and volunteers are certified and badged for the current year.
Confirm required tournament paperwork is complete, including that any player Tournament Absence forms are filled out by the parent (not a league officer).
Ensure AEDs, first aid kits, and medical releases are staged for each tournament team.
Submit/confirm the updated safety documentation with {{state}} {{district}} and report readiness to the board.

title: Send Oct 1 Abuse Awareness reset reminder
details: Notify all board members and volunteers that Little League's Abuse Awareness Training resets October 1 and must be re-completed for the coming year. On October 1 the annual nationwide background checks reset for the new season, and District Administrators/volunteers face a December 1 completion deadline with escalating reminders. Sending this reminder promptly kicks off the certification cycle so completions are tracked and badges can be issued in the spring.
steps: After the October 1 reset, send all board members and volunteers the reminder that Abuse Awareness must be re-completed for the new year.
Include the Little League University course link and instructions to select "{{communities}} LL" so completions tie to the league.
State the December 1 completion deadline and note prior-year completions do not carry over.
Ask recipients to forward their certificate and begin the JDP background check when invited.
Log responses in the certification tracker and send follow-up reminders to anyone outstanding.

title: Record meeting minutes and elections/positions roster
details:
Serve as recorder at board meetings (president typically facilitates): capture attendees/quorum, the positions and elections roster with owning role and term year, motions/votes (mover, seconder, amount/cap, outcome), and action items. Note any new positions created by motion.

The secretary serves as the recorder at board meetings while the president typically facilitates, producing the official record of who attended, what was decided, and who holds each office. This is the source of truth for the league's governance: the running Positions roster (with owning role and term year), the annual election results, and every motion/vote is captured here. It matters most at the fall/winter organizational meeting when officers are elected and new positions are created by motion, but a record is kept at each meeting throughout the year.
steps: Open the meeting's Google Doc agenda/record and fill the header: Facilitator, Recorder, and the full Attendees list; confirm quorum before votes are taken.

Work down the Positions roster, marking each voting officer and non-voting staff role as filled or 'Open,' and note the term year alongside each name (e.g., 'VP Softball effective 2027', 'Equipment Coordinator - 2026').
For every motion, record the mover, the seconder, any dollar amount or cap, and the outcome using the league's standard wording ('carried unanimously', 'unopposed', 'by unanimous decision').
Capture any newly created positions separately (e.g., a motion to create a Challenger VP role followed by a motion to elect someone to fill it) so both the creation and the election are on record.
Log all action items with the responsible person and due date under 'New Action Items,' and roll forward any open items from prior meetings.
Save the completed record in the shared Google Drive so it can be distributed and corrected by the board.

title: Distribute agenda and approved minutes to the board
details:
Compile and share the meeting agenda and notes via a document link after each meeting; solicit corrections and log omissions so the running minutes stay accurate.

After each board meeting the secretary shares the agenda and notes via a document link so members who attended (or missed the meeting) can review what was decided. Soliciting corrections keeps the running minutes accurate and creates an auditable record of motions, votes, and action items. This is a recurring post-meeting task done within a few days of every board meeting throughout the season.
steps: Finalize the meeting's agenda-and-notes Google Doc, ensuring attendees, motions/votes, the positions roster, and action items are all captured.
Set the document's sharing so board members can open the link, then email the board using the '{{leagueAbbrev}} - Meeting Agenda & Notes' pattern with the document link inserted.
Explicitly ask recipients to reply with any questions or omissions so the running minutes can be corrected.
Log any corrections or omissions members report back and update the shared doc so it remains the accurate record.
Keep the distributed link on file for reference at the next meeting when rolling forward open action items.

title: Review, update, and upload Constitution & By-laws to LLI
details:
Complete the recurring governance obligation: review the Constitution & By-laws, incorporate adopted policy changes, and upload the updated document to Little League International.

{{leagueAbbrev}} is a chartered Little League and must keep its Constitution & By-laws current on file with Little League International (LLI); the board treats this as a recurring governance obligation. This task incorporates any adopted policy changes into the governing document and re-submits it to LLI for acceptance. It sits early in the fiscal year so the league's charter documents are in order before the new season ramps up.
steps: Retrieve the current Constitution & By-laws and start from LLI's current sample constitution in the league's Data Center File Cabinet (the Regional office rejects documents that deviate too far from the template).
Incorporate any policy or structural changes the board has adopted since the last version (new board roles, division rules, etc.), keeping template language intact where required.
Route the document for the required officer signature using the league's e-signature workflow (Odoo) or a printed/signed copy as a fallback.
Submit the complete document through the LLI Data Center for Regional office review.
Watch for an acceptance or a 'Constitution Is Not Acceptable' notice from LLI; if rejected, address the noted areas against the sample template and resubmit until accepted.
File the accepted version in the league's shared drive and note completion in the board record.

title: Re-upload Constitution & By-laws after mid-season policy changes
details:
Refresh the governing documents on file with LLI following any adopted amendments (e.g., division rules, social media / advertising-sponsorship policy, new board roles) during the pre-season and in-season cycle.

When the board adopts amendments during the pre-season/in-season cycle (for example division rule changes, a social-media / advertising-sponsorship policy, or a newly created board role), the governing documents on file with LLI must be refreshed to match. This keeps the charter accurate mid-cycle rather than waiting for the year-end review. It is triggered by adopted motions, so it recurs whenever the board changes something material to the constitution or by-laws.
steps: Review recent board minutes to identify adopted amendments that affect the Constitution & By-laws (e.g., new positions created by motion, division rules, sponsorship/advertising policy).
Update the governing document from LLI's current sample constitution, folding in the adopted changes while preserving required template language.
Obtain the required officer signature via the e-signature workflow (Odoo) or a signed printed copy.
Re-submit the updated document through the LLI Data Center and resolve any Regional office rejection notices.
Replace the prior version in the league's shared drive and confirm the update to the board.

title: Year-end Constitution & By-laws review and upload
details:
Perform the closing-cycle review/update of the Constitution & By-laws and upload to LLI ahead of the Oct 1 fiscal-year reset.

The closing-cycle review of the Constitution & By-laws ensures the league's governing documents are current with LLI ahead of the Oct 1 fiscal-year reset. The board has repeatedly listed 'Constitution & By-laws - Required to be uploaded to LLI - Need review & update' on its fall organizational agendas, making this the annual governance checkpoint. It should be completed before the new charter year so the document is accepted in time.
steps: Pull the year's adopted amendments and the current on-file Constitution & By-laws for a full review against LLI's latest sample constitution.
Update the document to reflect the season's changes (new/retired board roles, elections outcomes, division and policy updates) using the current template as the baseline.
Route for the required officer signature via the league's e-signature workflow.
Submit through the LLI Data Center ahead of the Oct 1 fiscal-year reset and monitor for acceptance.
If LLI returns a 'not acceptable' notice, correct the flagged sections against the sample template and resubmit until accepted.
Archive the accepted year-end version and record completion in the fall meeting minutes.

title: Send Opening Day Snack Shack volunteer recruitment email
details:
Bulk-email a division's families to fill Snack Shack volunteer slots for Opening Day using the Sign Up Genius signup link; reiterate that children and players are not permitted in the snack shack for the event.

Opening Day is a full day of games and hungry patrons, so the snack shack needs adult volunteers to cover every slot from morning through evening. The secretary bulk-emails the division's families with the Sign Up Genius link to fill the openings and reiterates that children and players are not permitted in the snack shack for this event. This goes out in the days leading up to Opening Day (early May) and is often followed by reminders as slots remain open.
steps: Get the Opening Day snack shack Sign Up Genius link and confirm the field, date, and open/close hours from the concessions coordinator (e.g., Pennell Field, opens 8:30am, closes 8:00pm).
Draft the recruitment email using the 'Snack Shack Volunteers Needed - {{division}} Opening Day' template, filling in the division, day/date, field name, and hours.
Include the Sign Up Genius link and clearly state that children and players are NOT allowed in the snack shack for this event, since adult volunteers are required.
Mention the menu and that funds raised support the league to encourage sign-ups, and bulk-email the division's families.
Monitor the Sign Up Genius as Opening Day approaches and send follow-up reminders if slots remain unfilled.

links.label: Snack Shack Volunteers Needed - Opening Day

title: Prepare monthly treasury report for board meeting
details:
Compile current bank and PayPal/online balances, outstanding invoices/obligations, and P&L/budget notes to present at each board meeting.

The Treasurer presents a financial update at each board meeting so the board can make informed spending decisions and vote on motions with current cash position in hand. A typical report covers TD Bank and PayPal balances, outstanding invoices, and known obligations (e.g. Financial Update showing TD ~$31.9K / PayPal $10.1K, MSAD15 $300 rental outstanding, and a pending Fenway wall obligation in the 2023-01-08 agenda). Doing this before every meeting keeps the board's budget-vs-actuals current all season.
steps: Pull current balances from the league's TD Bank account and the PayPal/online donation account (and any Venmo/GoFundMe channels in use).
List outstanding invoices and receivables (e.g. facility/MSAD15 rentals) and known upcoming obligations still to be paid.
Summarize month-over-month P&L and note actuals against any approved 'up to $X' spending caps the board has authorized.
Send figures to the secretary ahead of the meeting so they appear in the agenda/notes doc under a 'Financial Update' section.
Present balances, outstanding items, and obligations at the meeting and answer questions before any spending motions are voted.

title: Pay Little League charter & insurance renewal
details:
Process the annual LL charter & insurance payment (Nov-Dec, ~$1,300; up to authorized cap of $2,000).

Each year the league must renew its Little League charter and insurance through the Little League Data Center, ideally by 12/31, to remain a chartered league able to field teams and All-Stars. The board authorizes the spend by motion each fall (e.g. 'Motion to authorize up to $2,000 for LL Charter & Insurance for 2022' in the 2021-12-12 agenda, with the actual cost running ~$1,300). Both general liability and accident insurance fees are built into the charter checkout, so following the prompts sets up coverage automatically.
steps: Confirm the board has authorized the spend by motion (historically up to a {{amount}} cap) at a late-fall meeting.
Log in to the Little League Data Center at https://apps.littleleague.org/dc/account/login before the 12/31 deadline.
Complete the charter renewal, following the prompts to add general liability and accident insurance rather than declining for external coverage.
Pay the charter and insurance fees (typically ~{{amount}}) from the league account.
Verify coverage via 'Manage Insurance/View Insurance Certificates' and confirm additional insured parties are listed.
Record the payment in the books and report it at the next board meeting.

links.label: Finance & Sponsorship - Budget Approval & Spending Controls

title: Reconcile registration revenue after open date
details:
Track registration fee receipts by division against the approved fee schedule after registration opens 1/1; flag earmarked funds (e.g. AAA+ increase for field repairs).

Registration is the league's primary revenue source, and fees are set by the board by motion; the Treasurer tracks receipts by division against the approved fee schedule once registration opens (typically 1/1). Reconciling early catches misapplied or missing payments and lets the board see revenue trends before uniform and equipment ordering. Earmarked components (such as an AAA+ increase dedicated to field repairs, or the Sandlot {{amount}} jersey add-on noted in the 2026-01-12 agenda) must be flagged and tracked separately from general funds.
steps: Confirm the approved fee schedule by division (including any non-volunteer fee and earmarked increases) from the board minutes.
Export registration receipts from the online registration platform and reconcile against PayPal/online deposits after the 1/1 open date.
Match paid registrations to the fee schedule by division and flag discrepancies, scholarships, or refunds.
Separate and tag earmarked funds (e.g. AAA+ increase for field repairs, Sandlot jersey add-on) so they are not treated as general revenue.
Report registration revenue-to-date by division in the monthly treasury report.

title: Track sponsorship payments and donor management
details:
Record sponsorship payments, manage donor tiers, and coordinate thank-you fulfillment (banners, plaques, signed/dye-sub jerseys); maintain donor records ({{donationPlatform}} subscription ~{{amount}}/yr).

The Treasurer records sponsorship and donation payments across all channels (checks, PayPal, Venmo, GoFundMe) in the Annual Sponsorship Log and coordinates fulfillment of donor recognition. This work supports uniform and banner ordering (sponsorships targeted no later than mid-February) and drives thank-you acknowledgements to larger donors (e.g. $250+ and $500+ highlighted for recognition). Donor records are maintained in {{donationPlatform}} (~$1,400/yr subscription), and the league completes corporate donation forms as required.
steps: Log each sponsorship/donation in the Annual Sponsorship Log with channel, amount, tier, and team/player preference from the Sponsorship Coordinator.
Reconcile incoming payments (checks to {{leagueMailingAddress}}, PayPal, Venmo, GoFundMe) against submitted sponsorship forms.
Maintain donor records in {{donationPlatform}} and complete any corporate donation forms with required naming/branding.
Flag larger donors ($250+ / $500+) for recognition and coordinate thank-you fulfillment (banners, plaques, jerseys) with the Coordinator.
Confirm sponsorships are received by mid-February so team and banner counts are final before the uniform order.
Send payment-request reminders to committed sponsors who have not yet paid.

title: Budget pre-season equipment and uniform spending
details:
Support equipment and uniform spending motions (e.g. up to $5,000 equipment, uniforms up to $18,000) and ensure approved caps are tracked against actuals.

Pre-season equipment and uniform purchases are the league's largest controllable spend, so the board approves them by 'up to $X' motions (e.g. up to $5,000 for equipment for the 2023 season, seconded and carried unanimously in the 2022-11-14 / 2023-01-08 agendas; uniforms up to $18,000). The Treasurer supports these motions by bringing cost detail to the board and then tracks actual spending against each approved cap. This keeps purchasing on budget through the winter/early-spring ordering window.
steps: Collect cost detail for the season's equipment and uniform needs (balls, cages, catcher's gear, helmets, jerseys) from equipment and uniform coordinators.
Present the itemized figures to the board so a member can make an 'up to $X' motion (e.g. up to $5,000 equipment, up to $18,000 uniforms).
Record the approved caps and the seconded/carried vote in the treasury tracking sheet.
As purchase orders and invoices come in, log actuals against each approved cap and flag any overrun before it happens.
Report equipment and uniform spend-to-date against caps in each monthly treasury report.

title: Establish tournament fundraising plan and goal
details:
Set the tournament/World Series fundraising goal and disbursement/per-diem plan (buckets, GoFundMe, business donations); confirm receipt and per-diem rules for the current cycle.

When All-Star teams advance to State and Regional (or World Series) play, travel becomes a major cost, so the league sets a fundraising goal and disbursement/per-diem plan to cover hotels, gas, and meals for advancing families and staff. Funds come from combined channels - donation buckets at partner businesses, GoFundMe, and business donations (e.g. a local PT center offering to 'cut you guys a check' for the 2023 New England Regional run). The plan confirms per-diem rules and any retained amount (e.g. 2024 Juniors: $11,135 raised, $2,520 retained for state-champion rings, remainder paid as $114.87/day per-diem shares).
steps: Estimate travel needs for the advancing team (nights of lodging, number of trips, meals) with the coach and president.
Set a fundraising goal and open the channels: donation buckets at partner businesses, a GoFundMe page, and direct business-donation outreach.
Confirm per-diem and disbursement rules for the cycle (per-day rate, shares per player family, any amount retained for rings/keepsakes).
Track incoming donations by channel toward the goal and keep a running total.
Report the fundraising total and proposed per-diem plan to the board/families before disbursing.

title: Collect donation buckets and check mailbox
details:
Empty donation buckets at partner businesses and check the league mailbox; log and deposit fundraising proceeds.

During a tournament run the league places donation buckets at partner businesses and collects mailed checks at the league PO Box; the Treasurer empties these, logs the proceeds, and deposits them toward the tournament fundraising goal. Regular collection keeps cash secure and gives an accurate running total for the per-diem calculation. Collection assignments are coordinated so every partner location is covered.
steps: Coordinate bucket-collection assignments so each partner business location is emptied on schedule.
Empty each donation bucket and check the league mailbox ({{leagueMailingAddress}}) for mailed checks and cash.
Count and log proceeds by source in the tournament fundraising tracker.
Deposit cash and checks promptly into the league account and record PayPal/Venmo/GoFundMe totals alongside.
Update the running fundraising total used for the per-diem disbursement calculation.

title: Disburse tournament family reimbursements
details:
Pay out hotel, per diem, and gas reimbursements to advancing tournament families per the approved stipend and receipt policy.

Once the fundraising total is set, the Treasurer pays out hotel, per-diem, and gas reimbursements to advancing tournament families and staff per the approved stipend plan. Amounts follow the disbursement rules confirmed for the cycle (e.g. 2024 Juniors Regionals: after retaining $2,520 for rings, the balance paid as $114.87/day for 5 days, $574.33 per share). Families choose to pick up checks (e.g. Sunday evening at the Douglas Snack Shack) or have them mailed.
steps: Finalize the total raised and subtract any board-approved retained amount (e.g. for championship rings).
Calculate per-share/per-diem amounts using the approved rate and number of eligible player families and staff.
Collect receipts for hotel and gas where the policy requires documentation before reimbursement.
Contact each family/staff member for their preferred payout method (pickup at the snack shack or mailed check).
Issue checks, log each disbursement against the fundraising total, and reconcile the tournament fund to zero (or note the remaining balance).

title: Request fall vendor samples and pricing
details:
Reach out to {{uniformVendor}}, Main Street Graphics, and {{equipmentVendor}} for current-season samples and price sheets, including girl's-cut softball jerseys, and outline jersey ordering deadlines.

Kicking off the uniform cycle in the fall, the coordinator gathers current-season samples and price sheets from the league's vendors so the board can compare options and set the coming season's uniform program. {{leagueAbbrev}} has historically sourced {{uniformVendor}} jerseys/hats for AAA and up, {{state}} Street Graphics for screen-printed shirts, and checked {{equipmentVendor}}, using samples as sign-up motivation. Doing this early (around October/November board meetings) leaves time to test fits at assessments and to check lead times before the ordering crunch.
steps: Contact {{uniformVendor}}, {{state}} Street Graphics, and {{equipmentVendor}} for current-season samples and printed price sheets, including a girl's-cut/softball-cut jersey option.
Ask each vendor about lead times and whether delivery windows change by season, plus minimum quantities for re-orders and the minimum-fee thresholds.
Request pricing for both dye-sublimated custom jerseys (name/number) and screen-printed shirts, plus hats, so per-division options can be compared.
Have samples ready to test at assessments/clinics and to use as sign-up motivation.
Summarize the sample and pricing findings for the board and outline the jersey ordering deadlines the calendar must accommodate.

title: Confirm early-signup jersey incentive terms
details:
Set the early-signup custom-uniform incentive and its Feb 15 deadline, and hand the details to registration/LIO for promotion.

To drive early registration, {{leagueAbbrev}} ties the custom-uniform perk to a hard early-signup deadline: families who register by the cutoff (Feb 15) are guaranteed a customized jersey, using uniforms as motivation for sign-ups. The coordinator finalizes those terms and hands them to registration/LIO so they can be promoted. This matters because earlier team formation makes ordering cheaper and simpler and keeps the season on schedule.
steps: Confirm the early-signup incentive (guaranteed customized jersey) and set the Feb 15 deadline with the board.
Nail down exactly which divisions/levels the custom-jersey perk applies to and what late registrants receive instead.
Write up the incentive terms clearly, including the no-exceptions nature of the customization cutoff.
Hand the finalized details to registration and the information officer/LIO for promotion on the website, email, and Facebook.

title: Compile vendor quotes and jersey layout
details: Ahead of the board decision, the coordinator assembles final vendor quotes, sponsor-on-front layout mockups, and per-division pricing into a single package for review. {{leagueAbbrev}}'s model has been sponsor names combined with the league logo on the front, player name/number on the back, roughly $28.50/set for screen-printed lower divisions (TB/CP/AA) and about $50/player {{uniformVendor}} plus Gilbert/college hats for AAA and up. Getting this right in late winter drives the spending motion and the timely order.
steps: Collect final written quotes from each vendor (e.g., {{state}} Street Graphics tiered pricing like 25 @ $28.50, personalization +$5; {{uniformVendor}} shirts/hats).
Build sponsor-on-front layout mockups: {{leagueAbbrev}} logo + sponsor on the front, player name and number on the back.
Assemble per-division pricing (e.g., ~$28.50/set for TB/CP/AA screen-print; ~$50/player {{uniformVendor}} + college/Gilbert hats for AAA and up).
Confirm extras such as coach matching jerseys and the +5 SB / +3 BB backup jersey counts, plus hat options for AA.
Package quotes, mockups, and pricing into a board-review document.

title: Present uniform purchase motion to the board
details: The coordinator brings the recommended vendor, team sizes, extras, and per-player budget to a board meeting for a formal spending motion so the order can be placed on time. {{leagueAbbrev}} has done this via specific motions (e.g., {{uniformVendor}} for AAA & Majors with {{leagueAbbrev}} logo, sponsor on front, name/number on back, matching MLB team hats). A recorded, seconded, carried motion authorizes the spend and locks the design before ordering.
steps: Add uniforms to the board meeting agenda with the recommended vendor and finalized design.
Present team counts per division, extras (backup jerseys, coach jerseys, hats), and the per-player budget.
Move a specific spending motion covering vendor, design details, and price increases; record the second and vote.
Capture any board-directed changes (e.g., opt-out pants at certain levels, hat approvals for AA/softball visors) in the minutes.
Confirm the authorized budget and design so the order can proceed on schedule.

title: Enforce customized-jersey deadline and finalize order
details:
Lock the 3/14 customized-jersey registration deadline, reconcile personalized vs. generic backup jerseys, and finalize team rosters for the order.

The coordinator locks the firm customized-jersey registration deadline (historically 3/14 / around 3/9), after which no exceptions are made, and reconciles who gets a personalized jersey versus a generic backup. This ties directly to team formation: teams are announced and rosters are finalized right before the order goes out. Getting this locked prevents costly re-orders of incorrect or extra jerseys.
steps: Enforce the firm customized-jersey registration deadline (e.g., 3/14) with no exceptions for late registrants.
Reconcile personalized jerseys against generic backup jerseys (planning the standard +5 SB / +3 BB extras).
Coordinate with the player agent/president so teams are finalized before ordering.
Cross-check each roster's name/number selections against registration data for accuracy.
Finalize team rosters and quantities so the order can be placed the following Monday.

title: Submit {{uniformVendor}} and hat orders
details:
Place the AAA-and-above {{uniformVendor}} order and Gilbert/hat order by the vendor cutoff; confirm coach adult-hat allotment per team.

Once rosters and sizing are locked, the coordinator places the AAA-and-above {{uniformVendor}} jersey order and the Gilbert/college-hat order by the vendor cutoff, typically the Monday after teams are announced. {{leagueAbbrev}} pays a deposit (25%) on the card to submit and confirms the coach adult-hat allotment per team. Hitting the vendor cutoff is what keeps uniforms arriving ahead of picture day and the season start.
steps: Finalize the {{uniformVendor}} order for AAA and Majors (and applicable softball levels) with confirmed names, numbers, and sizes.
Place the matching hat order (college/Gilbert or MLB-team hats, excluding Red Sox/Yankees) alongside the jerseys.
Include coach matching jerseys and confirm each team's adult-hat allotment (typically 3-4 per team).
Submit by the vendor cutoff and pay the required deposit (e.g., 25%) on the league card.
Note any rush add-ons needed and confirm expected delivery timing.

title: Run the uniform sizing event
details:
Send the sizing-event announcement, bring jersey and pant size samples, collect fit corrections, and submit final order adjustments by the deadline.

The coordinator holds an in-person sizing event (often at the batting cages) so families can try on jersey and pant samples and confirm fits before the order is finalized. {{leagueAbbrev}} also sends a selection form with size charts and notes learned patterns (e.g., girls'/women's styles run small and need to be sized up 1-2). This step exists because re-ordering incorrect uniforms is very expensive, so fit corrections are collected and submitted by a hard deadline.
steps: Send the sizing-event announcement with date, time, and location (e.g., the batting cages).
Distribute the online uniform selection form with jersey and pant size charts (defaulting to registration selections if not returned).
Bring jersey and pant size samples for players to try on, including youth/adult and girls'/women's cuts.
Collect fit corrections and note guidance (e.g., girls'/women's styles typically need +1-2 sizes).
Follow up with anyone who missed the session and submit final order adjustments by the stated deadline (e.g., Sunday 11:59pm).

title: Track uniform delivery against picture day
details:
Monitor vendor shipments and coordinate delivery timing with information_officer's picture/photo day so uniforms arrive first.

The coordinator monitors vendor shipments and coordinates delivery timing with the information officer's picture/photo day so that uniforms arrive before players are photographed. {{leagueAbbrev}} schedules photos around practices and needs teams in uniform (e.g., TB/CP pictures on a set Saturday), so uniforms must land first. Tracking shipments also gives time to place rush add-on orders for any missing or additional players.
steps: Confirm the photo/picture day dates with the information officer and identify which divisions are shooting when.
Track each vendor shipment's status and expected arrival against those photo dates.
Flag any at-risk deliveries early and place rush orders for missing or additional players as needed.
Ensure uniforms are sorted and available to teams before their picture day.
Communicate delivery timing to VPs/coaches so uniforms are distributed ahead of photos.

title: Coordinate coach uniform pickup and distribution
details:
Send the coach-pickup notice with day, time, and location; instruct one representative per team (not individual parents); provide storage access code; and send the youth-vs-adult hat clarification with coach adult-hat counts.

Once uniforms are sorted and bagged by team, the coordinator sends the coach-pickup notice with day, time, and location (historically the Douglas Field snack shack) and provides the storage lock code for off-hours pickup. Only one coach or team representative should collect the whole team's bagged, labeled uniforms, not individual parents. A follow-up clarifies youth vs. adult (OSFM) hats and the 3-4 coach adult-hat count per team.
steps: Sort, bag, and label uniforms by team and division (e.g., 'TB' vs 'CP' to avoid repeat team-name mix-ups).
Send the coach-pickup notice with day, time, and location, instructing one coach/rep per team (not individual parents).
Provide the snack-shack lock/storage access code for coaches who cannot make the pickup window.
Send the youth-vs-adult (OSFM) hat clarification, noting each team should have 3-4 adult hats for coaches.
Follow up with any teams that have not picked up so uniforms are distributed before pictures/first games.

title: Order All-Star uniforms
details:
Once All-Star rosters are voted, order team jerseys/uniforms at about {{amount}}/player per the approved per-player budget.

After All-Star rosters are voted and approved by the board, the coordinator orders team jerseys/uniforms at approximately {{amount}}/player per the approved per-player budget (a recurring board motion). This happens in June once managers and rosters are set, and numbers are assigned first-come as sizes are collected. Timely ordering matters so All-Star teams have uniforms before {{district}} tournament play.
steps: Wait for the board-approved All-Star rosters and the ~{{amount}}/player uniform budget motion.
Collect player names, sizes, and number preferences (numbers first-come, first-served).
Place the All-Star jersey/uniform order with the vendor at the approved per-player amount, adding a coach uniform.
Request a rush and pay the deposit if delivery timing is tight against tournament start.
Confirm delivery and distribute to the All-Star manager ahead of tournament play.

title: Procure Junior/Senior summer uniforms
details: The coordinator orders uniforms for Junior, Senior, and summer/tournament teams as advancing rosters are confirmed, which happens later than the spring order and often in smaller, add-on batches. {{leagueAbbrev}} collects roster info via an editable spreadsheet (name, adult size, number) and places rush orders (paying the deposit on the card) so teams are equipped quickly. Because these rosters firm up late, orders are turned around ASAP once players commit.
steps: Confirm the Junior, Senior, and summer/tournament rosters as advancing players commit.
Collect name, adult size, and number preferences via an editable roster spreadsheet (numbers first-come).
Place the uniform order, including any coach uniform, and request a rush if the season is imminent.
Pay the required deposit on the league card to submit the order.
Add any additional players in follow-up rush batches as late rosters change.

title: Update uniform vendor and pricing research
details: At season's end the coordinator refreshes the running uniform vendor/pricing research notes with this season's actual results (vendors used, quotes, lead times, minimums, fit lessons) to inform next year's sampling and ordering. {{leagueAbbrev}} maintains this as a carry-forward reference that reappears in successive board agendas. Capturing it while fresh avoids re-discovering the same pricing and lead-time details next fall.
steps: Record this season's final vendors, per-division pricing, and quantities actually ordered.
Note lead times, re-order minimums/minimum fees, and any delivery timing issues encountered.
Capture fit lessons learned (e.g., girls'/women's cuts running small, sizing-event adjustments).
Log which incentives/deadlines worked and any design decisions the board approved.
Save the updated notes to the shared research reference to seed next year's fall sampling.

title: Publish Junior & Senior baseball roster by Nov 1
details:
Send Junior & Senior baseball commitment letters, collect responses (due Nov 30), and publish the confirmed roster by Nov 1 so summer-team formation can begin early in the fiscal year.

Junior (13-14) and Senior (13-16) baseball are supplementary summer programs that play {{district}} towns after the middle-school/school season, so early commitment lets the league gauge whether it can field its own team or must combine with another town. Sending commitment letters in the fall and publishing a confirmed roster by Nov 1 gives summer-team formation a running start at the top of the fiscal year, well before spring registration crowds it out. Deadlines occasionally slide (e.g., to accommodate high-school showcase schedules), but the goal is a firm player count early.
steps: Draft and send commitment letters to eligible 13-16 baseball families explaining the Junior/Senior summer program, {{district}} opponents, and the June-July schedule window.
Set a firm response deadline (target Nov 30) and note it may extend if showcase or school schedules aren't out yet.
Track responses as they arrive to sense who is serious and estimate whether the numbers support a standalone team versus combining with a neighboring town.
Coordinate with the president / {{district}} administrator on whether {{leagueAbbrev}} fields its own Junior/Senior team or interleagues.
Confirm the roster and publish it by Nov 1 so summer-team formation and coach assignments can begin early.
Point families to the Juniors & Seniors division page for details and sign-up: {{infoWebsite}}/divisions/juniors-seniors

title: Rules / division review for baseball
details:
Contribute to the annual rules and division review (farm system, coach-pitch/player-pitch transition, age structure, playing-up) so baseball division rules are set before assessments and drafts.

Each fall/winter the board reviews baseball division structure - the farm/coach-pitch to player-pitch (AA) progression, age boundaries, and playing-up requests - so rules are locked before assessments and drafts. Setting these early ensures assessments evaluate players against the right division and that draft-eligible pools are correct. The VP Baseball contributes division-specific input (e.g., AA player-pitch pitching distance, strike-count rules, minimum lineup rules) that later flows into the playoff rules summary.
steps: Review last season's division definitions and any feedback on the coach-pitch/player-pitch (AA) transition and age structure.
Bring proposed baseball rule and division changes to a fall/winter board meeting for discussion (rules should be set before assessments).
Confirm AA player-pitch specifics that carry into playoffs (e.g., minimum pitching distance, strike counts, 8-player minimum lineup, per-pitcher inning/pitch limits).
Reconcile decisions with the {{leagueAbbrev}} Divisions reference and any playing-up policy so registration and assessments use the correct division boundaries.
Document the finalized baseball division rules and share with coaches, the player agent, and the scheduler ahead of assessments and the draft.

title: Book spring indoor practice time and schedule
details:
Secure gym/YMCA time and build the clinic-style indoor practice schedule for AA/AAA/Majors, coordinating coaches, assistant coaches, and volunteer setup crews for nets and bins.

Before fields are playable, {{leagueAbbrev}} runs clinic-style indoor sessions for AA/AAA/Majors at the {{leagueAbbrev}} middle school gym and at batting cage facilities (e.g., The Cages in {{townA}}). Securing gym/YMCA time and building the schedule keeps players developing through late winter and early spring, mostly with combined, skill-focused batting and fielding work. This requires coordinating head and assistant coaches plus volunteer setup crews for nets and equipment bins.
steps: Reserve gym/YMCA and cage time slots for AA/AAA/Majors and confirm dates for the indoor block.
Build a clinic-style schedule (hitting, fielding, drills) noting that most sessions are combined/skill-development rather than single-team.
Recruit head coaches, assistant coaches, and volunteer setup crews to run stations and set up/tear down nets and bins.
Communicate what players should bring - indoor shoes (no cleats), helmets, gloves, batting gloves, bats - and the facility locations.
Send the indoor-practice start announcement to families and post the schedule; roll into unit/team practices once fields open.

title: Coordinate post-draft practice/game schedule build
details:
After the draft and coaches meeting, work with the scheduler and coaches to finalize the baseball practice and game calendar leading into opening day (approx. April 10).

Once the draft and coaches meeting are done, teams exist and the calendar can be built for real. The VP Baseball works with the game/practice scheduler and coaches to finalize practices and games leading into opening day (approximately April 10). Getting this locked early lets coaches plan and lets families see a full schedule before the season starts.
steps: After the draft and coaches meeting, collect coach constraints (field access, blackout dates, preferred practice slots) for each AA/AAA/Majors team.
Work with the game and practice scheduler to draft the practice and game calendar toward an approx. April 10 opening day.
Reconcile field assignments against the Fields reference to avoid double-booking and account for shared fields.
Circulate a preliminary schedule to coaches for review and correct conflicts before publishing.
Finalize the calendar and hand off to coaches for entry into GameChanger.

links.label: Preliminary Schedule Draft for Review email

title: Enter and update baseball schedules in GameChanger
details:
Ensure AA/AAA/Majors coaches have entered practice and game schedules in GameChanger with correct start dates, fields, and times, and post league updates for families.

{{leagueAbbrev}} uses the GameChanger app as the single source for team rosters, schedules, and coach-to-family communication about changes and cancellations. The VP Baseball ensures AA/AAA/Majors coaches have entered practices and games with correct start dates, fields, and times, and that league updates reach families. Because GameChanger issues can delay roster/schedule posting, this needs active follow-up early in the season.
steps: Confirm rosters are posted so each AA/AAA/Majors team appears correctly in GameChanger.
Verify coaches have entered practices and games with accurate start dates, field names, and times.
Direct families to load their team using the {{registrationPlatform}} login and the GameChanger how-to FAQ.
Follow up on any GameChanger sync issues and have families reload their team once fixed.
Post league-wide schedule updates and keep GameChanger current as games are rescheduled or cancelled.

links.label: GameChanger for Rosters and Schedule email

title: Prepare baseball playoff schedule, brackets & rules
details:
Draw first-round matchups, build brackets (single vs double elimination by division), assemble the pitch-count and playoff rules summary, and coordinate the end-of-season BBQ / Home Run Derby with the president.

AA, AAA, and Majors playoffs run the first two weeks of June (typically starting ~6/3, most levels double elimination). The VP Baseball draws first-round matchups by random draw (placed on the regular schedule as the last set-opponent game), builds the brackets, and assembles the pitch-count and playoff rules summary. This task also includes planning consolation games and coordinating the championship-day BBQ / Home Run Derby with the president.
steps: Set playoff windows per level (AA/AAA/Majors) and decide format (double elimination, with a single-elimination fallback if weather disrupts).
Draw first-round matchups by random draw and place them on each team's schedule as the last game with a set opponent; add placeholders and consolation games.
Build complete brackets for online posting and note home-team rules (first round by coin flip; later rounds by playoff winning percentage).

Assemble the rules summary: mandatory pitch-count recording (including outside/travel pitching), forfeit for violations, AA player-pitch clarifications (pitching distance, strike counts, 8-player minimum, inning/pitch limits), and time limits for AAA/Majors except the championship.
Coordinate the championship-day BBQ / Home Run Derby date and logistics with the president.
Publish brackets to the playoffs page (e.g., {{infoWebsite}}/playoffs/playoffs-2026) and update GameChanger schedules.

links.label: Baseball Playoff Schedule, Rules & Brackets email

title: Send baseball playoff schedule/rules email
details:
Distribute the league-wide 'Baseball Playoff Schedule, Rules, & Brackets' announcement using the playoffs_tournament template with placeholders for dates, formats, distances, and the pitch-count link filled in.

This is the league-wide 'Baseball Playoff Schedule, Rules, & Brackets' announcement that goes to all AA/AAA/Majors families once brackets are drawn. It communicates start dates by level, the double-elimination format, the pitch-count requirement and rules link, AA player-pitch clarifications, consolation-game guidance, and championship-day BBQ details. It reinforces the positive-sportsmanship tone the league emphasizes for playoffs.
steps: Fill the playoffs_tournament template placeholders with per-level dates, format, AA pitching distance, and the pitch-count rules link.
Include the live brackets URL and note first-round matchups are already on schedules as the last set-opponent game.
Add rainout/flexibility language and the single-elimination fallback in case weather compresses the schedule.
Include consolation-game guidance (fun, low-stakes games and a medal ceremony for eliminated teams) and the championship-day BBQ / Home Run Derby details.
Send league-wide to AA/AAA/Majors families and confirm brackets are posted online before sending.

links.label: Baseball Playoff Schedule, Rules & Brackets email

title: Launch summer baseball registration and season
details:
Open summer baseball / summer-ball registration, set divisions and team counts, and stand up schedules and rosters for the summer program following the regular season.

After the regular season, {{leagueAbbrev}} stands up a summer program for AA/AAA/Majors that plays other {{district}} towns (Westbrook, Portland, Scarborough, Cape Elizabeth, Cumberland-North Yarmouth, etc.), typically running mid-July through mid-August with 2-3 games per week. Recent practice starts with an interest poll to see which levels can field teams before opening registration, then forms teams and builds schedules/rosters. Cost has run around {{amount}}/player when interest supports teams.
steps: Post an interest poll to gauge which levels (AA/AAA/Majors) have enough players to field summer teams.
Once interest is confirmed, open summer registration with a firm deadline and set the price (recently ~{{amount}}/player).
Set divisions, team counts, and the season window (recently ~July 13 - Aug 13, 2 games/week weekdays with optional Sunday games).
Confirm {{district}} interleague opponents and coordinate the cross-town schedule with the president/administrator.
Form rosters, assign coaches, and stand up schedules in GameChanger for the summer program.

title: Baseball season retrospective input
details:
Review end-of-season survey results and division feedback for baseball and summarize what went well / what to change for next year's structure, scheduling, and rules.

After the season, the board reviews end-of-season survey results and division feedback to decide what to keep and what to change for next year. The VP Baseball summarizes baseball-specific takeaways on structure, scheduling, and rules so improvements can be folded into the fall rules/division review. Capturing this while the season is fresh feeds the next year's planning cycle.
steps: Gather end-of-season survey results and coach/family feedback specific to the baseball divisions.
Summarize what worked and what to change for structure (division boundaries, playing-up), scheduling (game counts, indoor block, playoffs), and rules.
Note recurring pain points (e.g., GameChanger issues, weather/rainout impacts, pitch-count enforcement) with suggested fixes.
Present the baseball retrospective at a post-season/fall board meeting so decisions feed the rules/division review.
Record agreed changes to carry into next year's baseball planning.

title: Draft softball program improvement & recruitment plan
details:
Coming off the season, write up softball program improvements and a recruitment plan to grow numbers by division; flag any low-count divisions that may need interleague merger (e.g., Yarmouth softball, Windham Juniors).

Coming off the season, the VP Softball documents what worked and what didn't and lays out a plan to grow softball registrations by division for the next year. This matters because softball counts are thinner than baseball and low-count divisions (e.g., Yarmouth softball, Windham Juniors) may need interleague mergers to field viable teams. The plan sets the direction the softball parent group and board will execute against through the winter and spring.
steps: Pull the prior season's registration and team counts by division (AA/7-8, AAA/9-10, Majors/11-12, Juniors/12-16) and note where numbers are trending down.
Flag any division that cannot field enough teams and identify interleague partners to merge with (e.g., combine Juniors with Windham/Yarmouth) via {{district}} contacts.
List concrete program improvements from the season debrief - scheduling, field upgrades at Intervale, equipment gaps, high-school game opportunities, and social-media outreach.
Draft a recruitment plan with targets per division and outreach tactics (returning-player push, sibling sign-ups, scholarships/fee offsets, school flyers).
Bring the draft to the softball parent discussion group and full board for feedback, then finalize as the working plan for the season.

title: Coordinate winter softball clinics ({{instructorName}})
details:
Work with the president on scheduling the {{instructorName}} winter softball clinic - dates, gym space, age-group slots, session fees ($10/session or 4 for $30), and budget (~$2,600-$2,800, expected to break even).

Working with the president, the VP Softball books the winter softball clinics led by {{instructorName}} (former D1 pitcher / Colby pitching coach) with skills sessions from Madi Pelletier. Historically run over four Sundays starting mid-January (e.g., 1/19, 1/26, 2/2, 2/9 with a 2/16 weather makeup) at the {{indoorVenue}} gym. Session fees run around $10-15 each (4 for $30-45) with a budget near $2,600-$2,800 expected to break even, and scholarships offered on request.
steps: Confirm coach availability with {{instructorName}} (ages 9-12 pitching) and Madi Pelletier (all-levels skills) and lock four consecutive Sunday dates in mid-January with a weather-makeup date.
Reserve {{indoorVenue}} gym space and set age-group time slots (e.g., 1:30 AA ages 7-9, 2:30 AAA/Majors 9-12, 3:30 pitching 9-12).
Set session fees ($10-15/session, 4 for $30-45) and build a break-even budget (~$2,600-$2,800), noting full/partial scholarship offsets available on request.
Add clinic registration to the online sign-up alongside season registration and publish dates, times, and what players should bring (glove, bat, helmet, dry shoes).
Send reminders before each Sunday and post cancellations promptly if weather forces a move to the makeup date.

title: Plan softball team formation & assessments
details: Ahead of the spring draft, the VP Softball runs assessment stations and judges to rate players and forms preliminary teams across the 7-8 (AA), 9-10 (AAA), 11-12 (Majors), and 12-16 (Juniors) divisions. Assessments are typically held in late February with the board's registration/assessment process, feeding the draft that determines rosters. Solid team formation keeps divisions balanced and meets the Little League 12-game minimum needed for All-Star eligibility.
steps: Set assessment dates with the president (late February window) and reserve the cages/gym, planning a weather-postponement fallback.
Recruit volunteer judges and organize skill stations (throwing, fielding, hitting, pitching) with a consistent rating sheet per division.
Send the assessment schedule and reminders to registered softball families and confirm attendance.
Compile scores and draft preliminary balanced teams per division, coordinating with coaches and any interim schedulers.
Feed results into the draft process and hold rosters for board review before publishing.

title: Submit softball uniform & equipment requirements
details:
Give uniform and equipment coordinators softball specifics: girl's cut jerseys, softball-sized balls, catcher's gear, and league face masks required for all infield positions per the 2017 safety rule.

The VP Softball gives the uniform and equipment coordinators the softball-specific requirements so the correct gear is ordered on the tight March deadline. AAA and Majors players receive dye-sublimated custom jerseys with last name and number, so sizing must be confirmed before the order. Softball-sized balls, catcher's gear, and league face masks required for all infield positions per the 2017 safety rule must all be included; uniform orders have historically been due around March 20.
steps: Compile softball specifics for coordinators: girl's-cut jerseys, softball-sized balls, catcher's gear, and infield face masks per the 2017 safety rule.
Circulate the uniform sizing form (jersey and pants size charts) to AAA/Majors families to confirm sizes and numbers, with a firm due date (e.g., Sunday before the order).
Fall back to registration selections for any family that does not respond by the deadline.
Finalize team assignments so jerseys can be personalized, then release the order to the uniform coordinator by the March deadline (~March 20).
Confirm equipment counts (catcher's gear and masks per team) with the equipment coordinator and note any reorders to avoid costly mistakes.

title: Launch softball parent discussion group
details:
Kick off the bi-weekly softball parent/board discussion group; invite all softball parents, collect agenda items, and set the recurring meeting cadence and platform.

The VP Softball kicks off a bi-weekly softball parent/board discussion group to build a faster, more autonomous pathway for softball decisions instead of routing everything through the full board. The first meetings were held online via Google Meet (e.g., first meeting March 11, second April 1 at 7pm, moving to bi-weekly and later to 8/8:30pm once practices start). It's the engine for recruiting volunteers, planning purchases, and driving softball equitability and growth.
steps: Invite all softball parents and set a recurring bi-weekly cadence and platform (Google Meet), targeting ~1 hour per meeting.
Collect agenda items by email in advance and circulate an agenda plus notes from the prior meeting.
Cover standing topics: officer roles and volunteer recruitment, coming-season scheduling/travel, field improvements, equipment, uniforms, and high-school/{{district}} opportunities.
Track volunteer commitments to roles (VP Softball, Equipment, Concessions, Media, etc.) and open discussion items.
Adjust the meeting time later in the season (e.g., to 8:00-8:30pm) once practices begin, and keep notes for the board.

title: Organize Memorial Day parade softball participation
details:
Line up softball teams for the Memorial Day parade - notify families, coordinate banners, and confirm staging/route with the board.

The VP Softball lines up softball teams and families to march in the Memorial Day parade, giving softball visibility in both {{townA}} and {{townB}}. Historically there are reserved spots and staggered start times (e.g., {{townB}} meet at Memorial School 8:30 / step off 9:00; {{townA}} meet at Russell School 10:30 / step off 11:00), with candy for kids to throw. It's a community-facing event that promotes the league right in the middle of the season.
steps: Confirm reserved parade spots and staging/route for both towns with the board and secure a point person for each parade.
Notify softball families with meet times and locations and ask players to wear their jerseys.
Arrange banners and pick up bags of candy for kids to throw.
Coordinate wrangling volunteers to gather kids into the staging area so families know where to go.
Send a reminder the week of and confirm any parking arrangements with the board.

title: Coordinate District / high school softball game opportunities
details: The VP Softball pursues interleague, {{district}}, and high-school game and scrimmage opportunities to give softball players competitive reps and visibility. This includes the {{district}} college softball day (e.g., at SMCC) and coordinating with the local high school softball coach. Because other leagues book games early, softball needs VP representation at the district softball scheduling meetings (typically leading up to late March) to lock in the 12-game minimum for All-Star eligibility.
steps: Represent softball at {{district}} interleague softball committee meetings (aim for 2-3 sessions before the late-March scheduling meeting) via the {{district}} contact list.
Reach out early to neighboring leagues' softball VPs to secure interleague games/scrimmages before slots fill.
Coordinate with the high-school softball coach on scrimmages, clinics, and field-use opportunities.
Sign up for the {{district}} college softball day (e.g., SMCC) and communicate details to families.
Confirm each division reaches the 12-game minimum required for All-Star eligibility and share the finalized schedule.

title: Staff softball program roles for next year
details:
Recruit and confirm VP Softball, Softball Equipment, Softball Concessions, Media, and Scheduler positions; report the slate ahead of board elections.

Ahead of board elections, the VP Softball recruits and confirms the softball staff slate - VP Softball, Softball Equipment, Softball Concessions, Media, and Scheduler - so the program isn't dependent on a couple of informal volunteers. This directly addresses the gap where softball had no VP for multiple seasons and most operations ran unofficially. Reporting a confirmed slate lets the board seat officers cleanly during fall elections.
steps: Use the softball parent discussion group to canvass for volunteers and define/right-size each role.
Confirm commitments for VP Softball, Softball Equipment, Concessions, Media, and Scheduler, noting the effective year for each.
Fill any remaining gaps (e.g., grounds, purchase, uniform coordinators) and consider creating new roles by board motion if needed.
Document the slate and report it to the president/board ahead of the fall elections.
Hand off contacts and current responsibilities so incoming officers can start before the next season ramps up.
